[p. 326]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah An-Nahl (The Bee)

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah's command has come﴾.

That is, the time of the coming of the Resurrection has drawn near.

He expressed it in the past tense, treating the certainty of its occurrence as though it had already occurred. The nearness of the Resurrection indicated here, Allah, Majestic and Exalted, has explained in other places, such as His saying: ﴿The reckoning of mankind has drawn near for them, while they are heedless and turning away﴾ [al-Anbiya': 1]; His saying, Majestic and Exalted: ﴿The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split﴾ [al-Qamar: 1]; His saying: ﴿And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near﴾ [al-Ahzab: 63]; His saying: ﴿And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near﴾ [al-Shura: 17]; and His saying, Majestic and Exalted: ﴿The approaching one has approached; none besides Allah can remove it﴾ [al-Najm: 57-58], along with other verses.

The use of the past tense to refer to the future is common in the Qur'an, because of the certainty of its occurrence, such as His saying: ﴿And the Horn is blown, and whoever is in the heavens swoons﴾ and so on [al-Zumar: 68]; His saying: ﴿And the companions of Paradise call out to the companions of the Fire﴾ and so on [al-A'raf: 44]; and His saying: ﴿And the earth shines with the light of its Lord, and the Book is placed, and the prophets and witnesses are brought, and judgment is passed between them with truth, and they are not wronged. And every soul is paid in full for what it did, and He is most knowing of what they do. And those who disbelieved are driven﴾ and so on [al-Zumar: 69-71].

So all these past-tense verbs carry the meaning of the future, the certainty of their occurrence being treated as the occurrence itself.

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So do not seek to hasten it﴾. In this noble verse, Allah, Majestic and Exalted, forbids seeking to hasten what He has promised of terror and punishment on the Day of Resurrection. Seeking to hasten it means their asking that what they are promised of punishment on the Day of Resurrection be brought upon them sooner.

The verses clarifying this meaning are many, such as His saying, Majestic and Exalted: ﴿They ask you to hasten the punishment. Had there not been a specified term, the punishment would have come upon them, and it will surely come upon them suddenly while they are unaware﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 53]; His saying: ﴿They ask you to hasten the punishment, and indeed Hell encompasses the disbelievers﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 54]; His saying: ﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it, while those who believe are apprehensive of it﴾ [al-Shura: 18]; His saying: ﴿And if We delay the punishment from them for a counted period, they will surely say, "What is holding it back?"﴾ and so on [Hud: 8]; His saying: ﴿And they say, "Our Lord, hasten to us our portion before the Day of Reckoning"﴾ [Sad: 16]; and His saying: ﴿Say: Tell me, if His punishment comes upon you by night or by day, what is it that the criminals would hasten?﴾ [Yunus: 50], along with other verses.

Regarding the pronoun in His saying: ﴿So do not seek to hasten it﴾ [al-Nahl: 1], there are two interpretations in its explanation:

The first: it refers to the punishment promised for the Day of Resurrection, understood from His saying: ﴿Allah's command has come﴾ [al-Nahl: 1].

The second: it refers to Allah; that is, do not ask Allah to hasten the punishment for you. This was stated by Ibn Kathir.

Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (Qur'anic exegesis): Ibn 'Abbas said: When the verse ﴿The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split﴾ [al-Qamar: 1] was revealed, the disbelievers said, "This claims that the Resurrection has drawn near!" So they refrained from some of what they used to do. They waited and saw nothing, so they said, "We see nothing!" Then the verse ﴿The reckoning of mankind has drawn near for them﴾ [al-Anbiya': 1] was revealed, so they grew fearful and waited for the nearness of the Hour. The days lengthened, and they said, "We see nothing!" Then the verse ﴿Allah's command has come﴾ [al-Nahl: 1] was revealed, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims jumped up in alarm. Then ﴿So do not seek to hasten it﴾ was revealed, and they were reassured. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I and the Hour have been sent like these two," and he pointed with his two fingers, the index and the one next to it. End of the relevant part of al-Qurtubi's words. This indicates that the meaning of His saying ﴿So do not seek to hasten it﴾ is: do not presume it is occurring now in haste, but rather it is delayed until its appointed time with Allah, the Exalted.

As for the statement of al-Dahhak and those who agreed with him, that the meaning of ﴿Allah's command has come﴾ is His obligations and limits, it is a rejected statement with no basis. Imam Ibn Jarir al-Tabari refuted it in his tafsir, saying: It has not reached us that any of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sought to hasten the obligations before they were imposed upon them, so that it would be said to them on that account: "The obligations of Allah have come to you, so do not hasten them." As for those among the polytheists who sought to hasten the punishment, they were many. End of quote.

The apparent and immediate meaning of the noble verse is that it is a threat to the disbelievers with the nearness of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection, together with a prohibition against seeking to hasten it.

Ibn Jarir said in his tafsir: The most correct of the two views in my opinion is the view of the one who said: it is a threat from Allah to the people of disbelief in Him and His Messenger, and an announcement from Him to them that punishment and destruction are near to them. This is because He followed it with His saying: ﴿Glory be to Him, and high is He above what they associate﴾ [al-Nahl: 1], which indicates His rebuke of the polytheists and His warning to them. End of quote.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 2:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He sends down the angels with the Spirit of His command, upon whom He wills of His servants﴾.

The most apparent of the opinions regarding the meaning of "the Spirit" in this noble verse is that what is meant by it is revelation (al-wahy), because by revelation there is life of the spirits, just as by food there is life of the bodies. Supporting this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you a Spirit of Our command. You did not know what the Scripture was, nor what faith was﴾ [al-Shura: 52], and His saying: ﴿Raised in degrees, Possessor of the Throne. He sends down the Spirit of His command upon whom He wills of His servants, to warn of the Day of Meeting, the Day when they will come forth, nothing of them concealed from Allah. "To whom belongs the dominion this Day?" "To Allah, the One, the Subduer"﴾ [Ghafir: 15, 16].

Among what indicates that what is meant by "the Spirit" is revelation is that after His saying: ﴿He sends down the angels with the Spirit﴾ [al-Nahl: 2], there follows His saying: ﴿that warn﴾ [al-Nahl: 2], because warning is only by revelation, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿Say: I only warn you by revelation﴾ up to the end of the verse [al-Anbiya': 45]. Likewise, after His saying: ﴿He sends down the Spirit of His command upon whom He wills of His servants﴾ [Ghafir: 15], there follows His saying: ﴿to warn of the Day of Meeting﴾ up to the end of the verse [Ghafir: 15], because warning is also only by revelation.

Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read this letter as "yunzilu" (with a dammah on the yā', sukun on the nūn, and a light zāy), while the rest read it with a dammah and a shaddah (tashdid) on the zāy.

The word "min" [al-Nahl: 2] in the verse is either partitive (tab'idiyyah) or explanatory of the genus (li-bayan al-jins).

His saying: ﴿upon whom He wills of His servants﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 2], that is: He sends down the revelation upon whomever He chooses and knows to be fit for it.

As He, exalted is He, has clarified by His saying: ﴿Allah chooses messengers from the angels and from mankind﴾ [al-Hajj: 75];

• and His saying: ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾ [al-An'am: 124];

• and His saying: ﴿He sends down the Spirit of His command upon whom He wills of His servants﴾ [Ghafir: 15];

• and His saying: ﴿Wretched is that for which they have sold their souls, that they should disbelieve in what Allah has revealed, out of envy that Allah should send down of His bounty upon whom He wills of His servants﴾ [al-Baqarah: 90].

These verses and their like are a refutation of the disbelievers in their saying: ﴿Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a man of importance from the two cities?﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 31].

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That warn that there is no god but I, so fear Me﴾.

The most apparent reading of "an" in His saying "an andhiru" (that warn) is that it is the explanatory "an" (an mufassirah), because the sending down of the angels with the Spirit, that is, with revelation, carries the meaning of speech without its letters. So the meaning is: the revelation with which the angels were sent down is explained as warning mankind "there is no god but Allah" and commanding them to fear Him.

Exalted and majestic is He has clarified this meaning in many verses:

• such as His saying: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no god but I, so worship Me﴾ [al-Anbiya': 25];

• and His saying: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying]: Worship Allah and avoid Taghut﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 36];

• and His saying: ﴿And ask those whom We sent before you of Our messengers: Did We appoint gods besides the Most Merciful to be worshipped?﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 45];

• and His saying: ﴿Say: It is only revealed to me that your God is one God, so will you submit?﴾ [al-Anbiya': 108].

And other verses besides these. We have already set forth the meaning of warning (al-indhar) and the meaning of taqwa (God-consciousness).

**Al-Shinqiti's commentary (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 16, verse 4:**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He created man from a drop of fluid﴾.

In this noble verse, He, exalted and majestic, mentions that He created man from a drop (nutfah), which is the semen of the man and the semen of the woman. The evidence is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We created man from a drop of mingled fluid﴾ [al-Insan: 2], meaning mixtures of the man's water and the woman's water.

Sahib al-Durr al-Manthur (al-Suyuti) said, after mentioning some reports interpreting the word amshaj (mingled) as "mixtures": "from the water of the man and the water of the woman." Al-Tastari narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that Nafi' ibn al-Azraq said: "Tell me about His saying: ﴿from a drop, mingled﴾." He said: "The mixing of the water of the man and the water of the woman when it falls into the womb." He asked: "Do the Arabs know that?" He said: "Yes. Have you not heard Abu Dhu'ayb saying:"

*As if the feather and its two ends, through the notch of the arrow, were mixed with mashij.*

It is attributed in Lisan al-Arab to Zuhayr ibn Haram al-Hudhali, and he recited it thus:

*As if the arrowhead and its two ends from it, through the feathers, were smeared with mashij.*

He said: al-Mubarrad related it as:

*As if the shaft and the two sinews from it, opposite the arrowhead, were smeared with mashij.*

He said: Abu 'Ubayda related it as:

*As if the feather and its two ends from it, through the arrowhead, were smeared with the mashij.*

The meaning of "smeared with the mashij" is: mixed with it, a mixing.

Once you know the meaning of this, know that He, exalted is He, clarified that this water, which is the drop, has a part that comes out from the spine (sulb), meaning the man's water, and a part that comes out from the ribs (tara'ib), which is the woman's water. This is in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So let man look at what he was created from. He was created from a gushing fluid. It emerges from between the spine and the ribs﴾ [al-Tariq: 5–7]. [p. 331] By "spine" is meant the spine of the man, which is his back, and by "ribs" is meant the ribs of the woman, which is the place of the necklace on her. From this is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

*Slender, white-skinned, not overly plump, her ribs polished like a mirror.*

Ibn 'Abbas cited, in support of Nafi' ibn al-Azraq, that the tara'ib is the place of the necklace, with the saying of al-Mukhabbal, or Ibn Abi Rabi'a:

*Saffron on her ribs, and the breasts and the chest shone with it.*

So His saying here: ﴿from between the spine and the ribs﴾ [al-Tariq: 7] indicates that the amshaj are the mixtures mentioned. His command to man to look at what he was created from, in His saying: ﴿So let man look at what he was created from﴾ [al-Tariq: 5], is a reminder to him of the lowliness of what he was created from, so that he knows his worth and abandons arrogance and insolence. This is supported by His saying: ﴿Did We not create you from a despised fluid?﴾ and so on [al-Mursalat: 20].

He, exalted is He, clarified its lowliness by His saying: ﴿Does every one of them aspire to enter a garden of bliss? No! Indeed, We created them from what they know﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 38–39]. Expressing the drop with the relative pronoun "what" (ma) in His saying ﴿from what they know﴾ contains the utmost belittling of that origin from which man was created. In this is the greatest deterrent and the most eloquent rebuke against arrogance and self-exaltation.

* *

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and then he is an open adversary﴾ [al-Nahl: 4], the most apparent of the two views concerning it is that it is a reproach against the man mentioned. The meaning: We created him so that he would worship Us, submit to Us, and obey Us, yet he suddenly became a disputer and a denier, as indicated by the sudden-surprise "idha" (idha al-fuja'iyya, the "idha" of sudden occurrence). This meaning is clarified by His saying: ﴿I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 56], together with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Has man not seen that We created him from a drop, and then he is an open adversary? And he sets forth for Us a parable and forgets his own creation, saying, "Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?" Say, "He will give them life who produced them the first time, and He is Knowing of all creation"﴾ [Ya-Sin: 77–79],

and His saying: ﴿And He it is who created from water a human being and made him [a possessor of] lineage and marriage. And your Lord is ever Competent﴾ ﴿And they worship other than Allah that which neither benefits them nor harms them, and the disbeliever is ever an assistant [to Satan] against his Lord﴾ [al-Furqan: 54–55],

and His saying: ﴿And man says, "When I have died, will I then be brought out alive?"﴾ ﴿Does man not remember that We created him before, while he was nothing?﴾ [Maryam: 66–67],

and other verses besides these. Further clarification of this topic will come, God willing, in "Surat al-Tariq."

[p. 332] Note.

The scholars of Arabic grammar differed concerning the sudden-surprise "idha." Some said it is a particle (harf). Among those who held this was al-Akhfash. Ibn Hisham said in "al-Mughni": This view is favored by their saying: "I went out, and suddenly inna Zaydan is at the door" (with the kasra on inna), because "inna" with a kasra does not govern what comes after it over what comes before it. Others said it is an adverb of place (zarf makan), and among those who held this was al-Mubarrad. Others said it is an adverb of time (zarf zaman), and among those who held this was al-Zajjaj.

"Khasim" (khasim) is an intensive form (sigha mubalagha), meaning very contentious. It was said: "khasim" means "one who disputes." The use of the pattern fa'il in the sense of mufa'il (one who engages in an action with another) is frequent in the speech of the Arabs, as in qa'id in the sense of muqa'id (one who sits with another), jalis in the sense of mujalis (one who sits together with another), akil in the sense of mu'akil (one who eats together with another), and similar.

As for His saying: "mubin" [al-Nahl: 4], the apparent meaning is that it is the active participle of the intransitive "abana," in the sense of "bana" and "zahara" (became clear and manifest), meaning clearly contentious. From the use of "abana" in the sense of "bana" is the saying of Jarir:

*When our fathers and your father exceeded the limits, the mixed-breed camels became manifest among the purebred camels.*

That is, became manifest. And the saying of Umar ibn Abi Rabi'a al-Makhzumi:

*Even if an ant crawled over the surface of her skin, its traces from her would appear as swelling in the skin.*

He means: swelling in the skin would appear from their traces. It was also said: it derives from the transitive "abana," and the object is omitted, meaning: making its dispute clear and manifesting it. And God knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 5:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the cattle, He created them for you; in them is warmth and benefits, and from them you eat.﴾

In this noble verse, He - majestic and exalted - mentioned that He created the cattle for the children of Adam to benefit from them, as a favour from Him towards them. We have already mentioned in "Al 'Imran" that the Qur'an clarified that the cattle (al-an'am) are the eight pairs, which are: the male and female of the camel, the cow, the sheep and the goat. As for "warmth" (al-difu'), according to the more apparent of the two opinions, it is a name for that by which one is warmed, just as "filling" (al-mal') is a name for that with which something is filled, and it is the warmth of clothing made from the wool, hair and fur of the cattle.

What supports this is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Allah has made for you from your houses a place of rest, and He has made for you from the hides of the cattle tents which you find light on the day of your travelling and the day of your settling, and from their wool, their fur and their hair, furnishings and provision for a time.﴾ [An-Nahl: 80]. It was said: "warmth" means their offspring. The first is more apparent; and the offspring is included in His saying "and benefits" [An-Nahl: 5], i.e., from their offspring and their milk: ﴿and from them you eat﴾.

The benefits of the cattle, by which Allah - majestic and exalted - showed His favour upon His creation in this noble verse, He also explained to them in many other verses,

• such as His saying: ﴿And indeed, in the cattle there is a lesson for you: We give you to drink from what is in their bellies, and for you in them are many benefits, and from them you eat﴾ ﴿and upon them and upon the ships you are carried﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 21, 22],

• and His saying: ﴿It is Allah who made for you the cattle that you may ride some of them and from them you eat﴾ ﴿and for you in them are benefits, and that you may reach upon them a need in your breasts, and upon them and upon the ships you are carried﴾ ﴿and He shows you His signs, so which of the signs of Allah do you deny?﴾ [Ghafir: 79-81],

• and His saying: ﴿Do they not see that We have created for them, from what Our hands have made, cattle, and they are their owners?﴾ ﴿And We have subjected them to them, so some of them they ride and from some of them they eat﴾ ﴿And for them in them are benefits and drinks; will they not then be grateful?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 71-73],

• and His saying: ﴿And He who created all the pairs and made for you of the ships and the cattle that which you ride﴾ ﴿that you may sit upon their backs, then remember the favour of your Lord when you are seated upon them, and say: Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could not have subdued it, and indeed to our Lord we are returning﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 12, 13],

• and His saying: ﴿And He sent down for you of the cattle eight pairs﴾ [Az-Zumar: 6],

and other verses besides these.

The more apparent view regarding the i'rab (grammatical analysis) of "and the cattle" [An-Nahl: 5] is that its governing verb, which is "created," has been omitted in favour of the pronoun, so it is put in the accusative by a verb that is necessarily implied, explained by the mentioned "created," according to the saying of Ibn Malik in the Alfiyya:

"The preceding noun, put it in the accusative by a verb that is hidden, necessarily agreeing with what has appeared."

The accusative is more preferred here than the nominative because it is conjoined to the object of a verb, which is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He created man from a drop﴾ (the verse) [An-Nahl: 4]. So conjoining a verbal clause to a verbal clause is preferable to conjoining a nominal clause to a verbal clause if the preceding noun were put in the nominative. Ibn Malik pointed to this in the Alfiyya in his saying, conjoining to what is chosen to be in the accusative:

"And after a conjunction without separation upon the object of a verb established first."

Some scholars said: "and the cattle" is conjoined to "man" from His saying ﴿He created man﴾ [An-Nahl: 4]; but the first is more apparent, as you see.

The most apparent of the aspects of i'rab in His saying: ﴿for you in them is warmth﴾ [An-Nahl: 5] is that "warmth" is the subject (mubtada'), and its predicate (khabar) is "for you in them," and the beginning with an indefinite noun is permitted by its reliance on the preceding prepositional phrase, which is the predicate, as is well known; contrary to those who claimed that "warmth" is the agent (fa'il) of the prepositional phrase which is "for you."

In the verse there are other aspects which some scholars mentioned, which we have left out since they do not appeal to us; and knowledge is with Allah, may He be exalted.

His saying in this noble verse: ﴿and for you in them is beauty﴾ [An-Nahl: 6] means that keeping these cattle and owning them carries, for their owner among people, beauty; that is, majesty, elevation, and happiness in this world for those who keep them. Likewise He said regarding horses, mules and donkeys: ﴿that you may ride them, and as an adornment﴾ [An-Nahl: 8]. So He expressed with "beauty" regarding the cattle, and with "adornment" regarding others. "Jamal" is the verbal noun of "jamula," so he is "jamil" (beautiful) and she is "jamila" (beautiful). It is also said: she is "jamla'." Al-Kisa'i recited for this the poet's verse:

"She is jamla', like a rising full moon, she has surpassed all creation in beauty."

"Zina" (adornment) is that with which one adorns oneself. The Arabs used to take pride in horses, camels and the like, such as weapons, and did not take pride in cattle and sheep. What supports this is the saying of 'Abbas ibn Mirdas, boasting of the glorious deeds of his tribe, Banu Sulaym:

"Remember the trials of Sulaym in its battlefields, for in Sulaym is a source of pride for the people of pride."

"A people who supported the Merciful and followed the religion of the Messenger, while the affairs of people were in confusion."

"They do not plant the palm sapling in their midst, nor do cows low in their wintering."

"Except swift horses like eagles, made ready and close at hand, in an open space around which are the herds and the large camel herds."

"Al-sawabih" means horses. "Al-muqraba" means that which is prepared and made ready nearby. "Al-akhtar" is the plural of "khatr" (with fatha then sukun, or kasra then sukun), and it is a large number of camels, differing about its amount. "Al-'akar" (with two fathas) is the plural of "'akara," which is also a large herd of camels, differing about its determined amount. And the saying of another:

"By my life, indeed there is a people among whom yesterday you saw the stables for the mares and the abundant 'akar herds, more beloved to us than people in a high plateau, whose sheep are followed by the leopard."

His saying "al-'akar al-dathar" means abundant wealth of camels. He began with His saying ﴿when you bring them home﴾ [An-Nahl: 6], because that is the time of evening return, when their udders and bellies are fullest of them, at the time of their release to pasture.

The most apparent of the aspects of i'rab in His saying "and adornment" [An-Nahl: 8] is that it is an object of purpose (maf'ul li-ajlihi), conjoined to what precedes it; that is, for the sake of riding and adornment.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 8:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And He creates what you do not know﴾. In this noble verse, He - majestic and exalted - mentions that He creates what the addressees did not know at the time of its revelation, and He left vague what it is that He creates, by expressing it with the relative pronoun (al-mawsul). He did not explicitly specify anything of it here. However, the context of mentioning this in the setting of bestowing favour through mounts indicates that among it are things that are mounts. This has been witnessed in Allah's bestowal upon His servants of mounts that were not known at the time the verse was revealed, such as airplanes, trains, and automobiles.

This is supported by the Prophet's ﷺ allusion to this in the authentic hadith. Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj - may Allah have mercy on him - said in his Sahih: Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id, from 'Ata' ibn Mina', from Abu Hurayrah, that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "By Allah, the son of Maryam will certainly descend as a just judge, and he will certainly break the cross, and he will certainly kill the swine, and he will certainly abolish the jizyah, and the she-camels will certainly be abandoned so that none will be run after them, and enmity, hatred and envy will certainly disappear, and they will certainly call to wealth, but no one will accept it." End of quotation.

The point of evidence in this authentic hadith is his ﷺ saying: "and the she-camels will certainly be abandoned so that none will be run after them." This is an oath from the Prophet ﷺ that camels will be abandoned and none will be pursued on them, and this is observed now due to the independence from riding them by the mounts mentioned.

In this hadith there is a great miracle that indicates the truth of his ﷺ prophethood, although his miracles - may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him - are too numerous to be enumerated.

This indication we have mentioned is called the indication of concomitance (dalalat al-iqtiran, i.e., inference from juxtaposition), and most of the scholars of legal theory (usul) have deemed it weak, as indicated by the author of Maraqi al-Su'ud in his saying:

"As for the juxtaposition of wording in what is well known, it does not equate in anything other than what is mentioned."

Some scholars have held it valid as a proof. Our purpose in using it as evidence here is that the mention of ﴿And He creates what you do not know﴾ [al-Nahl: 8] in the context of bestowing favour through mounts is no less than an indicator showing that the verse points to some of the mounts being part of what is intended by it, as its correctness has become apparent by direct observation.

It has been mentioned in another place that He creates what His creation does not know, without being linked to the favour of mounts, and that is in His saying: ﴿Glory be to the One who created all the pairs, from what the earth grows, and from themselves, and from what they do not know﴾ [Ya-Sin: 36].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 9:

The saying of the Exalted: ﴿And upon Allah is the directing of the way, and of it is deviating﴾. Know first: "qasd al-sabil" [An-Nahl: 9] means the straight, direct road, which has no crookedness in it. This meaning is well known in the speech of the Arabs, and from it is the saying of Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma al-Muzani: (p-336)

"Her heart has become sober of Salma, and its falsehood has ceased, and the steeds of youth have been stripped bare,

and its mounts; and I have desisted from what you know, and there has been fixed upon me, other than the directing of the way, its guide."

And the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

"And of the path is a deviating one, and a guidance, the directing of the way, and of it is one with a bend."

Having known this, know that in the meaning of the noble verse there are two well-known aspects held by the scholars, and each of them has a correspondence in the Book of Allah, except that one of them is more apparent to me than the other. The first of them: the meaning of ﴿And upon Allah is the directing of the way﴾ is that the paths of truth, which are the directing of the way, are upon Allah, that is, they lead to Him, not deviating or swerving from reaching Him and His good pleasure. ﴿And of it is deviating﴾, that is, and of the path is a deviating one that does not reach Allah, but rather is crooked and swerving from reaching Him. What supports this meaning is His saying the Exalted: ﴿And that this is My straight path, so follow it, and do not follow the ways, lest they separate you from His way﴾, and His saying: ﴿And that worship Me; this is a straight path﴾. What confirms this interpretation is His saying after it: ﴿And of it is deviating﴾. This aspect is more apparent to me, and Ibn Kathir and others preferred it, and it is the saying of Mujahid. The second aspect: the meaning of the noble verse, ﴿And upon Allah is the directing of the way﴾, that is, it is incumbent upon Him, Majestic and Exalted, to make clear to you the path of truth through the tongues of His messengers. What indicates this aspect is His saying the Exalted: ﴿Messengers as bearers of good tidings and warners, so that people will have no argument against Allah after the messengers﴾, and His saying: ﴿And We would not be punishing until We send a messenger﴾, and His saying: ﴿And upon Our Messenger is only the clear delivery﴾, along with other verses. According to this view, the meaning of His saying ﴿And of it is deviating﴾ is not clear, because the meaning would be: and of the path is one deviating from the truth, which is what Allah has forbidden you to take. "Al-jair" is the one inclining away from the path of truth. The two aspects mentioned in this verse also apply to His saying: ﴿Indeed, upon Us is the guidance﴾ ... the verse.

The saying of the Exalted: ﴿And had He willed, He would have guided you all﴾. In this noble verse, Majestic and Exalted has made clear that if He willed the guidance of all His creation, He would have guided them all, and He clarified this meaning in other verses, such as:

• His saying: ﴿And had Allah willed, He would have gathered them upon guidance, so do not be among the ignorant﴾ [Al-An'am: 35],

• and His saying: ﴿And had We willed, We would have given every soul its guidance﴾ ... [As-Sajdah: 13],

• and His saying: ﴿And had Allah willed, they would not have associated﴾ [Al-An'am: 107],

• and His saying: ﴿And had your Lord willed, those on earth would have believed, all of them together﴾ ... the verse [Yunus: 99],

• and His saying: ﴿And had your Lord willed, He would have made mankind one nation﴾ ... the verse [Hud: 118],

along with other verses. We have already presented this in "Surah Yunus".

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 13:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And what He has created for you on the earth, varying in its colors. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who remember.﴾

His saying: "وما" [al-Nahl: 13] is in a position of accusative (naṣb) by way of conjunction (ʿaṭf) with His saying: ﴿And He subjected for you the night and the day﴾. That is: and He subjected for you what He created for you on the earth, that is, what He created for you therein while its colors are varying.

In this noble verse, He, may He be glorified and exalted, mentions His favor upon His creation by what He subjected for them of what He created for them on the earth, alerting that His creating what He created for them on the earth, together with the great blessings in it, contains a clear proof for whoever remembers and takes heed of His oneness and of His being entitled to be worshipped alone.

He repeated this meaning in many places, such as:

• His saying: ﴿It is He who created for you all that is on the earth﴾ [al-Baqarah: 29], the verse;

• and His saying: ﴿And He subjected for you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, all from Him﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 13], the verse;

• and His saying: ﴿And the earth He laid out for the creatures. Therein is fruit, and palm trees having sheaths. And grain having husk, and fragrant plants. So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?﴾ [al-Rahman: 10–13], and His saying: ﴿It is He who made the earth tractable for you, so walk among its slopes and eat from His provision; and to Him is the resurrection﴾ [al-Mulk: 15].

In this noble verse He also indicates that the variation of the colors of what He created on the earth, among humans, animals and others, is among the greatest proofs that He is the Creator of every thing, and that He alone is the Lord, the one deserving to be worshipped alone.

He clarified this in other verses, such as His saying in "Surat Fatir": ﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down from the sky water, and We bring forth thereby fruits varying in their colors? And among the mountains are white and red streaks of varying colors, and [some] extremely black. And among people and creatures and livestock are those of varying colors likewise﴾ [Fatir: 27], and His saying: ﴿And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth and the variation of your languages and your colors﴾ [al-Rum: 22]. There is no doubt that the variation of colors, appearances, measures, forms and other things contains a decisive proof that Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, is One, having no likeness, no equal, and no partner, and that He alone is the one worshipped.

It also contains a decisive proof that every influence is by the power and will of the choosing agent, and that nature does not influence anything except by His will, may He be glorified and exalted.

As He clarified this in His saying: ﴿And on the earth are neighboring tracts and gardens of grapevines and crops and palm trees, some multiple and some single, watered with one water; and We make some of them exceed others in fruit. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason﴾ [al-Ra'd: 4]. The land in which the fruits grow is one, since its plots are adjacent; the water with which they are irrigated is one water; yet the fruits come out differing in excellence, varying in colors, shapes, tastes, measures and benefits.

This is the greatest decisive proof of the existence of a choosing agent who does what He wills in the manner He wills, glorified and exalted above partners and rivals.

Among the clearest proofs that nature does not influence anything except by His will, may He be glorified and exalted: fire, despite the intensity of its natural property of burning, had wood cast into it while Ibrahim (ʿalayhi wa ʿalā nabiyyinā al-ṣalātu wa al-salām) was in it. There is no doubt that wood is harder, sturdier and stronger than the skin and flesh of Ibrahim. So the fire burned the wood with its heat, and it was coolness and peace upon Ibrahim, when its Creator said to it: ﴿We said, "O fire, be coolness and peace upon Ibrahim"﴾ [al-Anbiya': 69]. Glory be to Him who nothing occurs, whatever it may be, except by His will, may He be glorified and exalted, the Doer of what He wills.

His saying in this noble verse: يَذَّكَّرُونَ [al-Nahl: 13]; its original form is يَتَذَكَّرُونَ (yatadhakkarūna), in which the tā' was assimilated into the dhāl (idghām). And al-idekār (al-idhkār/remembrance, here "remembering") means taking heed (iʿtibār) and being admonished (ittiʿāẓ).

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 14 (part 1 of 5):

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It is He who subjected the sea, that you may eat from it fresh meat and extract from it ornaments which you wear, and you see the ships plowing through it, and that you may seek of His bounty, and perhaps you will be grateful.﴾ [p. 343] In this noble verse, He, may He be glorified and exalted, mentions that He subjected the sea, meaning He made it submissive to His servants so that they could ride it and benefit from what is in it, such as hunting and ornaments, and reach the regions that the seas would otherwise prevent them from reaching, in order to obtain profits from trade and the like.

The subjugation of the sea for riding is among the greatest of God's signs, as He explained in other places, such as His saying: ﴿And a sign for them is that We carried their offspring in the laden ship, and We created for them from its likes that which they ride﴾ (Ya-Sin 36:41-42), and His saying: ﴿It is God who subjected the sea to you so that ships may sail upon it by His command and that you may seek of His bounty and perhaps you will be grateful﴾ (al-Jathiyah 45:12), along with other verses.

In this verse He mentioned four of His blessings upon His creation through the subjection of the sea to them:

The first: His saying: ﴿that you may eat from it fresh meat﴾ (an-Nahl 16:14). He repeated the favour of this blessing in the Qur'an, such as His saying: ﴿Lawful for you is the game of the sea and its food as a provision for you and for the travellers﴾ (al-Ma'idah 5:96), and His saying: ﴿and from each you eat fresh meat﴾ (Fatir 35:12).

The second: His saying: ﴿and extract from it ornaments which you wear﴾ (an-Nahl 16:14). He also repeated the favour of this blessing in the Qur'an, such as His saying: ﴿From both emerge pearls and coral. So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾ (ar-Rahman 55:22-23). "Pearls and coral" are the ornaments which they extract from the sea for wearing. And His saying: ﴿and from each you eat fresh meat and extract ornaments which you wear﴾ (Fatir 35:12).

The third: His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿and you see the ships plowing through it﴾ (an-Nahl 16:14). He repeated in the Qur'an the favour of cleaving the waves of the sea for ships, such as His saying: ﴿and We created for them from its likes that which they ride. And if We willed, We would drown them, and there would be no one to answer their cry, nor would they be saved﴾ (Ya-Sin 36:42-43), and His saying: ﴿and He subjected for you the ships to sail through the sea by His command﴾ (Ibrahim 14:32).

The fourth: seeking of His bounty through profits from trade by means of carrying goods on ships, which is mentioned in His saying here: ﴿and that you may seek of His bounty﴾ (an-Nahl 16:14), meaning, as the profits of trade. He also repeated the favour of this blessing in the Qur'an, such as:
• His saying in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿and the ships that sail through the sea with that which benefits people﴾ (al-Baqarah 2:164),
• and His saying in Surat Fatir: ﴿and you see the ships plowing through it, that you may seek of His bounty and perhaps you will be grateful﴾ (Fatir 35:12),
• and His saying in Surat al-Jathiyah: ﴿It is God who subjected the sea to you so that ships may sail upon it by His command and that you may seek of His bounty and perhaps you will be grateful﴾ (al-Jathiyah 45:12),
along with other verses.

* *

[p. 344] Issues related to this noble verse:

The first issue: There is no implied contrary meaning (mafhum al-mukhalafah, the argument that a restriction implies the opposite ruling for what is not restricted) from His saying: ﴿fresh meat﴾ (an-Nahl 16:14). So it should not be said that the restriction to being fresh implies that dried meat of what is in the sea, such as qadid (sun-dried meat), is not permissible to eat. Rather, eating qadid of what is in the sea is permissible by the consensus (ijma', the agreement of the scholars) of the scholars.

It has been established in the principles of jurisprudence (usul al-fiqh) that among the impediments to considering the implied contrary meaning is that the text is delivered to express a favour (imtinan). For it was restricted to fresh meat only because it is the best of it, so expressing the favour through it is more complete.

The author of Maraqi al-Su'ud has pointed to this, saying, enumerating the impediments to considering the implied contrary meaning: "Or a favour, or agreement with reality, or ignorance, or emphasis for the hearer." The point of evidence is his saying "or a favour," and we have already mentioned this in Surat al-Ma'idah.

* *

The second issue: Know that the scholars of the Malikiyyah (the Malikis) derived from this noble verse that the meats of everything in the sea are one genus (jins); therefore, it is not permissible to exchange one for another with differences in quantity in sale, nor to sell its fresh for its dried, because they are one genus.

They said: Because God expressed all of them with a single word, which is His saying in this noble verse: ﴿It is He who subjected the sea, that you may eat from it fresh meat﴾ (an-Nahl 16:14), and it encompasses everything in the sea.

From here the scholars of the Malikiyyah made the meats of four genera, with no fifth for them:
The first: the meat of everything in the sea is one genus, for what we have mentioned.
The second: the meats of the quadrupeds of the livestock (an'am) and the wild animals are all, according to them, one genus. They said: Because God differentiated between their names during their life, so He said: ﴿of the sheep two and of the goats two﴾ (al-An'am 6:143), then He said: ﴿and of the camels two and of the cattle two﴾ (al-An'am 6:144). As for after their slaughter, He expressed them by a single name, so He said: ﴿Lawful for you are the beasts of grazing livestock﴾ (al-Ma'idah 5:1), thus He gathered them under one meat. And many scholars said: The wild animals such as gazelles enter into "the beasts of grazing livestock."
The third: the meats of birds of all their kinds are one genus, because of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿and meat of birds of whatever they desire﴾ (al-Waqi'ah 56:21), [p. 345] thus He gathered their meats under one name.
The fourth: locusts (al-jarad) are, according to them, one genus. We have already mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah the indication of the disagreement about their status as ribawi (subject to the rules of riba, usury, in exchange). The well-known position of Malik is that they are not ribawi, based on the view that the prevalence of food as sustenance is among the components of the effective cause ('illah) of riba, for the effective cause of riba in ribawi items according to Malik is: being a staple food (iqtiyat) and being storable (idikhar). It was said: and prevalence as sustenance. We have already mentioned that the disagreement about requiring prevalence as sustenance has a practical effect in four things: locusts, eggs, figs, and olive oil, and we have already mentioned the details of this in Surat al-Baqarah.

When you know this, then know that each genus of these mentioned genera may be sold for the other genus with differences in quantity, hand to hand (yadan bi-yad, immediate exchange). And selling its fresh for its dried is permissible, hand to hand, also in the school of Malik, may God have mercy on him.

The school of Imam Abu Hanifah, may God have mercy on him: meats follow their origins, so every meat is an independent genus like its origin. So camel meat is, according to him, an independent genus, and likewise goat meat and beef, and so on, because meats follow their origins, and the origins differ, like flours and oils.

As for the school of al-Shafi'i and Ahmad in this issue, both have two narrations from them. As for the two narrations from al-Shafi'i: the first is that all meats are one genus, because they share the specific name which is "meat" (lahm). The second is that they are genera according to their origins, like the position of Abu Hanifah.

The author of al-Muhadhdhab said: This is the position of al-Muzani, and it is the correct one.

As for the two narrations in the school of Imam Ahmad: the first is that all meats are one genus. This is the apparent meaning of al-Khiraqi's words, for he said: "And all other meats are one genus." The author of al-Mughni said: Abu al-Khattab and Ibn 'Aqil mentioned it as a narration from Ahmad. Then he said: Al-Qadi Abu Ya'la denied that this is a narration from Ahmad, and said: The livestock animals, the wild animals, birds, and aquatic animals are genera, and differences in quantity are permitted among them by unanimous narration, and the two narrations concern only meat. The first: it is four genera as we have mentioned. The second: it is genera according to the differences in their origins. End of quotation from al-Mughni with slight editing, omitting what is unnecessary. These then are the positions of the four schools on this issue.

The one who wrote this commentary, may God pardon and forgive him, says: The disagreement of the scholars on this issue is from the disagreement over the realization of an effective cause (tahqiq manat) from the texts of the Sharia. This is because it is established in Sahih Muslim and others, from the hadith of ['Ubadah ibn al-Samit], may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "When these kinds differ, then sell as you wish, provided it is hand to hand." So it is known that the difference of the two categories is the effective cause for permitting differences in quantity.

And their unity is the effective cause for prohibiting differences in quantity. The disagreement of the scholars is over the realization of this effective cause. Some of them say: meat is one genus, expressed by one name, so the effective cause for prohibiting differences in quantity exists in it. Others say: these are meats of differing genera, because they come from animals of differing genera, so the effective cause for prohibiting differences in quantity does not exist. And God knows best.

* *

The third issue: It is not permissible to sell meat for a live animal of the same genus that is edible.

This is the position of the majority of scholars, among them Malik, al-Shafi'i, and Ahmad. Abu Hanifah, may God have mercy on him, said: It is permissible to sell meat for a live animal, because the live animal is not ribawi, so it resembles selling it for money.

The majority argued with what Malik narrated in al-Muwatta', from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, that the Messenger of God ﷺ "forbade selling meat for a live animal." Also in al-Muwatta', from Malik, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn: that he heard Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab say: "Of the gambling of the people of the Jahiliyyah is selling a live animal for meat, for a sheep or two sheep." Also in al-Muwatta', from Malik, from Abu al-Zinad, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: that he used to say: "It was forbidden to sell a live animal for meat." Abu al-Zinad said: I said to Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: "What do you think of a man who bought a she-camel in its prime (shaarif) for ten sheep?" Sa'id said: "If he bought it to slaughter it, then there is no good in that." Abu al-Zinad said: "Everyone I encountered among the people used to forbid selling a live animal for meat." Abu al-Zinad said: "This used to be written in the instructions to the officials in the time of Aban ibn 'Uthman and Hisham ibn Isma'il, forbidding that." End of quotation from al-Muwatta'.

Ibn Qudamah said in al-Mughni: There is no disagreement in the school that it is not permissible to sell meat for a live animal of its genus. This is the position of Malik and al-Shafi'i, and the view of the seven jurists of Madinah. It is reported from Malik that it is not permissible to sell meat for a live animal that is fattened for meat, but it is permissible for other than that. Abu Hanifah said: It is permissible absolutely, because he sold an item of riba for something that is not riba, so it resembles selling meat for dirhams, or for meat of another genus.

Our evidence is what is reported: that the Prophet ﷺ "forbade selling meat for a live animal," narrated by Malik in al-Muwatta', from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from the Prophet ﷺ. Ibn 'Abd al-Barr said: This is the best of its chains. It is also reported from the Prophet ﷺ: "that he forbade selling a living thing for a dead one," mentioned by Imam Ahmad. It is reported from Ibn 'Abbas: "that a slaughtered camel was brought, and a man came with a she-goat, and said: Give me a portion for this she-goat. Abu Bakr said: This is not permissible [p. 347]." Al-Shafi'i said: I know of no one who disagreed with Abu Bakr in that. Abu al-Zinad said: Every one of them I encountered forbade selling meat for a live animal. And because meat is a type in which riba exists, and it was sold for its origin which contains the same thing, so it is not permissible, like selling sesame for sesame oil (shirij). End of quotation.

The author of al-Muhadhdhab said: It is not permissible to sell an animal whose meat is eaten for its meat, because of what Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, may God be pleased with him, narrated: that the Prophet ﷺ said: "A living thing is not sold for a dead one." And Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, narrated: "that a slaughtered camel was brought in the time of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, and a man came with a she-goat and said: Give me meat for it. Abu Bakr said: This is not permissible." And because it is a genus in which riba exists, and it was sold for its origin which contains the same thing, so it is not permissible, like selling sesame oil for sesame. End of quotation.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 14 (part 2 of 5):

Ibn al-Subki said in his *Takmilah* (Supplement) to the *Sharh al-Muhadhdhab*: The hadith of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab was narrated by Abu Dawud through the route of al-Zuhri, from Sa'id, as the author (al-Nawawi) mentioned. Malik narrated it in the *Muwatta'*, and al-Shafi'i in the *Mukhtasar* and the *Umm*, and Abu Dawud through the route of Zayd ibn Aslam, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: that "the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) «forbade the sale of meat for a live animal»." This is the wording of al-Shafi'i from Malik, and of Abu Dawud from al-Qa'nabi, from Malik. It is also the same in the *Muwatta'* of Ibn Wahb. I saw in the *Muwatta'* of al-Qa'nabi, "«the sale of a live animal for meat»," and the meaning is one. Both hadiths, I mean the narration of al-Zuhri and that of Zayd ibn Aslam, are *mursal* (a hadith in which a Successor relates directly from the Prophet (ﷺ), omitting the Companion), and none of them traced it back to Sa'id (as a connected chain). It has been narrated through other routes, among them from al-Hasan, from Samurah: that "the Prophet (ﷺ) «forbade that a sheep be sold for meat»." Al-Hakim narrated it in the *Mustadrak*, and said: "All of its narrators are imams, memorizers, and trustworthy." Al-Bukhari relied on al-Hasan's narration from Samurah, and it has a *mursal* corroborating witness in the *Muwatta'*. This is the statement of al-Hakim. Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in his *Sunan al-Kubra* and said: "This is a sound chain." Whoever establishes that al-Hasan heard from Samurah counts it as *mawsul* (connected). Whoever does not establish it considers it a good *mursal* that is joined to the *mursal* of Sa'id. Among the routes is that from Sahl ibn Sa'd, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) «forbade the sale of meat for a live animal»." Al-Daraqutni narrated it and said: "Yazid ibn Marwan alone transmitted it from Malik with this chain, and he was not followed in it. Its correct form in the *Muwatta'* is from Ibn al-Musayyab as a *mursal*." Al-Bayhaqi mentioned it in his *Sunan al-Saghir* and ruled that this was an error of Yazid ibn Marwan. Yazid, the one mentioned, was criticized by Yahya ibn Ma'in. Ibn 'Adi said: "This is not among the well-known (narrations)." Among the routes is that from Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Prophet (ﷺ) «forbade the sale of a live animal for meat». 'Abd al-Haqq said: "al-Bazzar narrated it in his *Musnad* through the narration of Thabit ibn Zuhayr, from Nafi'. Thabit was a man from the people of Basrah, of disputed narrations (munkar al-hadith), and cannot stand alone with it. Abu Hatim al-Razi mentioned this." The end of the relevant point from the words of the author of the *Takmilat al-Majmu'*.

(p-348)

The compiler of these notes, may Allah pardon him, said: It is not hidden that what we have mentioned establishes the prohibition of selling meat for a live animal. As for the view of those who accept *mursal* hadiths, such as Malik, Abu Hanifah, and Ahmad, there is no difficulty. As for the view of those who do not accept *mursal* hadiths, the *mursal* of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab is a proof according to many who do not accept *mursal* hadiths, especially since it is strengthened by the hadith of al-Hasan from Samurah. According to the view of those who consider al-Hasan's hearing from Samurah sound, there is no difficulty in its authenticity, because it is then a sound, connected hadith. As for the view of those who do not establish al-Hasan's hearing from Samurah, its lowest level is that it is a sound *mursal*, strengthened by a sound *mursal*. Such a hadith is relied upon by those who accept *mursal* hadiths and by those who do not. We have previously discussed, in "Surah al-Ma'idah," the statements of the scholars on al-Hasan's hearing from Samurah. We also previously mentioned, in "Surah al-An'am," that such a *mursal* is relied upon without disagreement by the Four Imams. Thus it is clear from these texts that selling a live animal for meat of its own kind is not permissible, contrary to Abu Hanifah. As for when it is of a different kind, such as selling a sheep for fish meat, or a bird for camel meat, it is permissible according to Malik, because *muzabanah* (the sale of an unknown quantity of one thing for a known quantity of the same kind by estimation) is eliminated by the difference of kind. The meaning of the hadith is understood in this way, although its apparent meaning is general. The position of al-Shafi'i regarding a difference of kind has two opinions: One: the permissibility of selling meat for a live animal when their kinds differ. The second: an absolute prohibition, because of the generality of the hadith. Ahmad's position on this question was mentioned by Ibn Qudamah in *al-Mughni* in his words: "As for selling meat for an animal of a different kind, the apparent statement of Ahmad and al-Kharaqi is that it is not permissible. For Ahmad was asked about selling a sheep for meat, and he said: 'It is not valid, because the Prophet (ﷺ) «forbade that it be sold even for a dead animal».' Al-Qadi preferred its permissibility, and al-Shafi'i has two opinions on it. Those who prohibited it argued from the generality of the reports, and because all meat is one kind. Those who permitted it said: 'A ribawi item has been sold without its origin or its kind, so it is permissible, as if he had sold it for currency.' If he sold it for an animal that is not eaten, it is permissible according to the apparent statement of our companions, and this is the view of the majority of jurists." End of the words of the author of *al-Mughni*.

The compiler of these notes, may Allah pardon him, said: You have learned from what preceded that some scholars said all meat is one kind, and some said that meats are different kinds. Based on the view that all meat is one kind, the prohibition of selling a live animal for meat is the apparent ruling. Based on the view that meats are different kinds, the apparent ruling regarding selling meat for an animal of a different kind is permissibility, due to his (ﷺ) saying: «When the kinds differ, sell as you wish.» And knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted.

(p-349)

Note.
The Malikis stipulated, in the prohibition of selling a live animal for meat of its own kind, that the meat not be cooked. If it is cooked, its sale for a live animal of the same kind is permitted according to them, and this is the meaning of the words of Khalil in his *Mukhtasar*: "and what is forbidden is invalid unless there is evidence, such as an animal for its own kind's meat if it is not cooked." They argued for this: that cooking transforms the meat away from its kind, so disparity between it and uncooked meat is permissible, and therefore selling it for a live animal is all the more permissible. Thus they say. And knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted.

* *

The fourth issue: Know that the apparent meaning of this noble verse indicates that it is permissible for a man to wear a garment adorned with pearls and coral, because Allah, Exalted is He, said in it, in the context of a general favor upon His creation, coupled with eating: ﴿and that you may extract from it ornaments which you wear﴾ [al-Nahl: 14]. This address is addressed to males, as is well known. A parallel to this is His saying, Exalted is He, in Surah Fatir: ﴿And from each you eat fresh meat, and extract ornaments which you wear﴾ [Fatir: 12]. Al-Qurtubi said in his *Tafsir*: Allah, Glorified is He, bestowed a general favor upon men and women with what comes out of the sea, so nothing from it is forbidden to them. He, Exalted, only forbade men gold and silk. Ṣāḥib al-Insaf (al-Mardawi) said: It is permissible for both men and women to adorn themselves with jewels and the like, and this is the correct view within the school. Some scholars held that it is not permissible for a man to wear a garment adorned with pearls, for example. I know of no basis for the prohibition except the generality of the hadiths carrying a severe warning against men imitating women, and the reverse. Al-Bukhari said in his *Sahih*: "Chapter: Men who imitate women and women who imitate men." Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: «The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cursed the men who imitate women and the women who imitate men.» This hadith is a clear, explicit text that the imitation of men with women is forbidden, because the Prophet (ﷺ) curses no one except for committing a act that is severely forbidden. And there is no doubt that when a man wears pearls and coral, he has imitated women. If it is said: The verse must be given precedence over this hadith and what resembles it from hadiths, for two reasons:
First: the verse is a *mutawatir* (widely transmitted) text, and the hadith mentioned is a *khabar ahad* (solitary report), and the *mutawatir* takes precedence over the solitary.

(p-350)

Second: the hadith is general regarding all kinds of imitation of women, while the verse is specific in permitting the ornament extracted from the sea, and the specific takes precedence over the general. The answer: We have not seen anyone address this. What appears to us, and Allah the Exalted knows best, is that although the noble verse is stronger in its chain and more specific to the point of dispute, the hadith is stronger in its indication of the point of dispute than it. The strength of indication in a text suitable for argument on the point of dispute outweighs the strength of the chain, because His saying: ﴿and that you may extract from it ornaments which you wear﴾ [al-Nahl: 14] may strongly mean that the favor in it is that their women adorn themselves for them with it, so their pleasure and enjoyment in that beauty and adornment arising from that ornament is among the blessings of Allah upon them. The attribution of wearing to them is because they benefit from it and take pleasure in their wives wearing it. By contrast, the hadith is an explicit text that does not admit of another meaning regarding cursing those who imitate women. And there is no doubt that a man adorned with pearls, for example, imitates them. So the hadith undoubtedly covers him. Ibn Hajar said in *Fath al-Bari*, in commenting on the aforementioned hadith, and it has been used as evidence that it is forbidden for men to wear a garment adorned with pearls, and this is clear, because of the indications of prohibition present, which is the curse upon whoever does that. As for al-Shafi'i's statement: "I do not dislike a man wearing pearls, except that it is a women's style," it does not contradict this, because his intention is that no specific prohibition regarding it has been reported.

* *

The fifth issue: It is not hidden that drinking from vessels of silver and gold is prohibited absolutely. It is also not hidden that it is permissible for women to wear gold and silk, and it is prohibited for men. This is one of the matters on which there is no disagreement, because of the abundance of sound texts explicitly stating it from the Prophet (ﷺ), and the consensus of the Muslims on this. Whoever deviates from this is refuted by the explicit texts and the consensus of those among the Muslims whose agreement is considered. We will mention a small portion of the many texts related to this.

As for drinking from their vessels: al-Shaykhan (al-Bukhari and Muslim), Imam Ahmad, and the authors of the *Sunan* narrated from Hudhayfah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: «Do not drink from vessels of gold and silver, nor eat from their dishes, for they are theirs in this world and yours in the Hereafter.» The wording «nor eat from their dishes» is in Sahih Muslim. And from Umm Salamah, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: «Indeed, the one who drinks from a silver vessel is only swallowing the fire of Hell into his belly.» Agreed upon. In a narration of Muslim: «Indeed, the one who eats or drinks from a vessel of gold and silver is only swallowing the fire of Hell into his belly.» And the hadiths of this kind are numerous.

As for wearing silk and *dibaj* (brocade), which is a type of silk: from Hudhayfah, may Allah be pleased with him (p-351), who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: «Do not wear silk or brocade, and do not drink from vessels of gold and silver, for they are theirs in this world and yours in the Hereafter.» Narrated by al-Shaykhan and the rest of the group. And from 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: «Do not wear silk, for whoever wears it in this world will not wear it in the Hereafter.» Agreed upon. And from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him: that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: «Whoever wears silk in this world will not wear it in the Hereafter.» Also agreed upon. The hadiths of this kind are very numerous.

The commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 14 (part 3 of 5):

As for men wearing gold, al-Shaykhan (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated in their two Sahihs, on the authority of al-Bara' ibn Azib (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Prophet (ﷺ) "forbade them from the gold ring." Al-Bukhari said in his Sahih: Adam narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, Ash'ath ibn Sulaym narrated to us, who said: I heard Mu'awiyah ibn Suwayd ibn Muqrin say: I heard al-Bara' ibn Azib (may Allah be pleased with both of them) say: "The Prophet (ﷺ) forbade us from seven things: he forbade the gold ring, or he said the gold ring-hoop, and silk, brocade (istabraq), dibaj, the red saddle-cloth (mithara), al-qassiy, and silver vessels. And he commanded us to seven things: visiting the sick, following funeral processions, blessing the one who sneezes, returning greetings, answering the summons of the inviter, fulfilling the oath of the one who swears, and helping the oppressed."

The wording in Muslim's Sahih is close to this, except that Muslim placed the seven commanded things before the seven forbidden things. In his narration he said: "And he forbade us from rings, or from wearing a ring of gold." This agreed-upon hadith indicates that wearing gold is not permissible for men, because if it is forbidden in the ring, then other forms of it are more deserving of prohibition. It is almost known as a matter of religion by necessity, and the reports on this are numerous.

As for the permissibility of women wearing silk, there are many proofs for it, among them the hadith of Ali (may Allah be pleased with him): "I gifted the Prophet (ﷺ) a silk striped garment (hullah siyara). He sent it to me, so I wore it, and I recognised anger in his face. He said: 'I did not send it to you for you to wear it; I sent it to you so that you would tear it into headscarves (khumur) among your women.'" (Agreed upon.) Also from Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him): that he saw on Umm Kulthum, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), a striped silk garment. This was narrated by al-Bukhari, al-Nasa'i and Abu Dawud. The reports of this kind are numerous. The permissibility of silk for women is known as a matter of religion by necessity. The dissent of Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr (may Allah be pleased with both of them) on this has no weight, because he is refuted by the authentic texts and by the agreement of the majority of the scholars of the Muslims.

As for the permissibility of women wearing gold, many reports have come concerning it. Among them is what Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, al-Hakim (who declared it sahih), and al-Tabarani narrated on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari (may Allah be pleased with him): that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Gold and silk are made lawful for the females of my ummah, and forbidden for its males." In this hadith there is some discussion, because its narrator from Abu Musa is Sa'id ibn Abi Hind, and some scholars said: he did not hear from Abu Musa.

The author of this (al-Shinqiti) (may Allah pardon him) says: Even if we assume that he did not hear from him, the hadith is still a proof, because it is a mursal (a hadith in which the Companion is omitted from the chain), reinforced by many other hadiths, some of which are hasan and others whose chains are close to it, as al-Hafiz (Ibn Hajar) explained in al-Talkhis. It is also supported by the consensus (ijma') of the Muslims. Al-Bayhaqi (may Allah have mercy on him) said in his al-Sunan al-Kubra: "Chapter: the citing of reports indicating the prohibition of adorning oneself with gold," and he cited hadiths on this. Then he said: "Chapter: the citing of reports indicating its permissibility for women," and then he cited hadiths on that, including the hadith of Sa'id ibn Abi Hind mentioned above from Abu Musa. Then he said: "We also narrated it from the hadith of Ali ibn Abi Talib, Uqbah ibn Amir, and Abdullah ibn Amr, from the Prophet (ﷺ)." He also mentioned the hadith of Aisha, who said: "A jewelry piece (hilyah) came to the Prophet (ﷺ) from al-Najashi, who had sent it to him, and in it was a gold ring. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took it with a stick, turning away from it, or with some of his fingers. Then he called Umamah, the daughter of Abu al-As, the daughter of his daughter Zaynab, and said: 'Adorn yourself with this, little daughter.'" He also mentioned the hadith of the daughter of As'ad ibn Zurarah (may Allah be pleased with him): "She and her two sisters were in the care of the Prophet (ﷺ), because their father had entrusted them to him. She said: So the Prophet (ﷺ) would adorn us with gold and pearls." In another narration: "He would adorn us with gold earrings (ri'ath) and pearls." In another narration: "He would adorn us with gold ingots (tibr) and pearls."

Then al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Ubayd said: Abu Amr said: The singular of ri'ath is ru'thah, and ru'athah, and it is the earring (qurt). Then al-Bayhaqi said: These reports and what has come with a similar meaning indicate the permissibility of adorning oneself with gold for women. We took as evidence the occurrence of consensus on its permissibility for them as a basis for abrogating (naskh) the reports indicating its prohibition specifically for them. Some scholars have said: the agreement of the consensus (ijma') with a solitary report (khabar al-ahad) makes it definitive (qat'i), because it is reinforced by the definitive, which is the consensus. This was discussed previously in "Surat al-Tawbah." And Allah knows best.

It is therefore established that there is no doubt about the prohibition of wearing gold and silk for men, and their permissibility for women.

* *

The sixth issue: As for men wearing silver rings, it is permissible without any doubt, and its evidences are well known in the Sunnah. Among the clearest of them is the ring of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), made of silver, on which was engraved: "Muhammad, Messenger of Allah," which Abu Bakr wore after him, then Umar, then Uthman, until it fell into the well of Aris, as is established in the two Sahihs. As for men wearing other than the ring made of silver, there is a difference of opinion among the scholars, and we will clarify this issue, if Allah wills.

Know first: if a man wears silver of the kind women wear as jewelry, such as anklets, bracelets, earrings, necklaces, and the like, then this should not be a matter of disagreement regarding its prohibition, because it is imitation (tashabbuh) of women. Whoever among men imitates them is cursed by the tongue of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), as has passed just above. And whoever is cursed by his tongue (ﷺ) is cursed in the Book of Allah, as Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) said, because Allah says: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it﴾ [al-Hashr: 7].

As for other matters, such as a man putting silver in a garment, or a man using an item adorned with one of the two precious metals, the majority of scholars, including the four Imams, hold that this is prohibited, along with the consensus (ijma') on the permissibility of a man wearing a silver ring. There is disagreement on some things, such as the belt (mintaqah), weapons of war and the like, and the Qur'an mushaf. There is agreement on the permissibility of making the nose-piece of gold, and of binding teeth with gold and silver. We will mention some texts from the branches (furu') of the four schools on this.

Khalil ibn Ishaq al-Maliki said in his Mukhtasar, in the chapter where he stated what the fatwa is based on, the following text: "It is forbidden to use an adorned male item, even a belt and a weapon of war, except the sword and the nose-piece, binding a tooth in any way, and a silver ring; not that which is partly gold even if little, and a gold vessel and keeping it, even for a woman. And in the plated (mughashsha), the coated (mamawwah), the banded (mudabbab), the one with a hoop (dhi al-halqah), and a vessel of jewels, there are two opinions. It is permissible for a woman to wear anything at all, even a sandal, but not a bed." End of the purpose of Khalil's words, with some difference in some of the issues he mentioned according to the Malikis.

The author of Tabyin al-Haqa'iq in the school of Imam Abu Hanifah said the following text: "A man may not adorn himself with gold or silver, except with a ring, a belt, and the silver sword-hilt." End.

Al-Nawawi said in Sharh al-Muhadhdhab in the school of al-Shafi'i: "Chapter on what is permissible and forbidden of ornaments." Gold in its origin is prohibited for men and permissible for women, until he said: As for silver, it is permissible for a man to wear a ring of it, and whether he may have other silver ornaments such as the armlet (dumluj), the bracelet, the torque, and the crown, there are two opinions. The majority definitively ruled for prohibition. End of the relevant part of al-Nawawi's words.

Ibn Qudamah said in al-Muqni' in the school of Imam Ahmad: "It is permissible for men to wear a silver ring. As for the adornment of a belt, there are two narrations, and by analogy with it the coat of mail (jawshan), the helmet (khudhah), the sock (khuff), the stirrup-strap (ran), and the sword straps (hamail). From gold, the pommel of the sword (qabi'at al-sayf). It is permissible for women to wear of gold and silver everything that their custom is to wear, whether little or much." End of the relevant part of al-Muqni'.

From these quotations it has become clear that the four Imams are generally in agreement on prohibiting the use of items adorned with gold or silver, whether garments, tools, or other things, except for items they excepted, with some differences among them regarding some of them.

Some scholars said: wearing anything of silver is not prohibited. Those who said this relied on two matters. The first: no prohibition has been established regarding it. The author of al-Insaf, in explaining the words of the author of al-Muqni' ("and by analogy with it the coat of mail and the helmet, etc."), said the following text: "The author of al-Furu' said regarding it: I do not know of a clear text from Ahmad on the prohibition of silver. The words of our shaykh indicate the permissibility of men wearing it, except what the Sharia has indicated is prohibited." End. Shaykh Taqi al-Din also said: "Wearing silver, when there is no general text on it, no one is entitled to prohibit it, except what the legal evidence has established as prohibited. So when the Sunnah permitted the silver ring, this indicates the permissibility of what is similar to it, and what is more deserving of permissibility than it. What is not like that requires consideration regarding its permissibility or prohibition, and prohibition requires evidence, while the default is its absence." The author of al-Furu' supported this and rejected all the evidence the followers of the school relied on. End of the words of the author of al-Insaf.

The second matter: a hadith from the Prophet (ﷺ) indicates this. Abu Dawud said in his Sunan: Abdullah ibn Maslamah narrated to us, Abd al-Aziz (i.e., Ibn Muhammad) narrated to us, from Usayd ibn Abi Usayd al-Barrad, from Nafi' ibn Ayyash, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever loves to make his beloved a ring of fire, let him make for her a ring of gold; and whoever loves to make his beloved a necklace of fire, let him make for her a necklace of gold; and whoever loves to make his beloved a bracelet of fire, let him make for her a bracelet of gold. But upon you is silver, so play with it." This is the wording of Abu Dawud.

The author of this (al-Shinqiti) (may Allah pardon him) says: What appears to me, and Allah knows best, is that this hadith contains no proof for the permissibility of men wearing silver. Whoever cites this hadith as evidence for the permissibility of men wearing silver has erred. Rather, the meaning of the hadith is that gold was forbidden to women, and that the Prophet (ﷺ) forbade men from adorning their women with gold, and said to them: "Play with silver," meaning: adorn your women with it as you wish. Then after that the prohibition of gold for women was abrogated (naskh). The evidence for what we have mentioned consists of several matters:

The first: the hadith is not addressed to men regarding what they themselves wear, but regarding what they adorn their beloveds with, and the intended ones are their women. This is because the Prophet (ﷺ) said in it: "Whoever loves to make his beloved a ring," "to necklace his beloved," "to bracelet his beloved." He did not say: whoever loves to make himself a ring, or to necklace himself, or to bracelet himself. So this clearly indicates, without any ambiguity, that the intended meaning of his words "play with it" is: adorn your beloveds with it however you wish, because the end of the speech is connected to its beginning.

The second matter: it is not the custom of men to wear gold rings, nor to wear gold necklaces, nor to wear gold bracelets, generally; so this indicates that what is intended is one whose custom is to wear the ring, the necklace and the bracelet of gold, and they are women without doubt.

The third matter: Abu Dawud (may Allah have mercy on him) said after the aforementioned hadith, directly connected to it: Musaddad narrated to us, Abu Awanah narrated to us, from Mansur, from Rib'i ibn Khirash, from his wife, from a sister of Hudhayfah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O assembly of women, do you not have in silver something with which you may adorn yourselves? Indeed, there is no woman among you who adorns herself with gold and displays it, except that she will be punished for it."

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 14 (part 4 of 5):

Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, saying: Aban ibn Yazid al-'Attar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, that Muhammad ibn 'Amr al-Ansari narrated to him, that Asma' bint Yazid narrated to him: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Any woman who wears a necklace of gold, a necklace of its kind will be hung around her neck from the Fire on the Day of Resurrection, and any woman who puts a gold earring in her ear, a similar one will be put in her ear from the Fire on the Day of Resurrection."

These two hadiths indicate that what is meant by the first hadith is the prohibition of gold for women, and that his saying, "so play with them" (fa-al'abu biha), means: so permit your women silver to adorn themselves with as you wish, as is clear in the last two hadiths. This is very clear, as you see.

It is also supported by the fact that the hafiz al-Bayhaqi (may Allah have mercy on him) mentioned the three hadiths, among which is "and upon you is silver, so play with it," in the context of the hadiths indicating the prohibition of gold for women first, without silver. Then after that he mentioned the hadiths indicating abrogation (naskh), then said: "We have inferred, from the occurrence of consensus (ijma') on its permissibility for them, the abrogation of the reports indicating its prohibition for them specifically. And Allah knows best." End of quote.

Among those hadiths is the hadith "so play with it," and it is very clear regarding what we have mentioned. If it is said: his saying (ﷺ) in the aforementioned hadith, "he would encircle his beloved," "that he would put a necklace on his beloved," "that he would put a bracelet on his beloved," indicates that what is meant is a male, because had he meant a female he would have said "habibatahu" (his beloved, feminine) with the feminine ta' to distinguish between male and female.

The answer: The application of the word "habib" (beloved) to a female, on account of intending the beloved person, is widespread in the speech of the Arabs and there is no difficulty in it. From it is the saying of Hassan ibn Thabit (may Allah be pleased with him):

"Worries have prevented sleep at nightfall, and an apparition when the stars grow jealous (i.e., at night).
From a beloved who struck your heart with an ailment, and it is hidden, concealed within."

And what he means by "beloved" is a female, as shown by his saying after it:

"The sun of day has not taken from her anything, except that youth does not last."

And the saying of Kuthayyir 'Azzah:

"If the coldness of water were a lover thirsting towards me, a beloved, she is indeed a beloved (habib)."

And the like of this is abundant in the speech of the Arabs, so we will not prolong the discussion with it.

The author of these notes (may Allah pardon him and forgive him) says: What appears to me from the Book of Allah, Exalted and Most High, and the Sunnah of His Prophet (ﷺ) is that wearing silver is forbidden for men, and that whoever among them wears it in this world will not wear it in the Hereafter. The clarification of this is that al-Bukhari said in his Sahih, in the chapter "On men wearing silk and the amount of it that is permitted": Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from Ibn Abi Layla, who said: "Hudhayfah was in al-Mada'in, and he asked for water.
