A dihqan (a Persian landowner) brought him water in a silver vessel. He threw it at him and said: 'I did not throw it except that I had forbidden him, but he did not desist.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Gold, silver, silk and brocade are theirs in this world, and yours in the Hereafter.'"

So the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) in this authentic hadith: "Gold, silver, silk, and brocade: they are theirs in this world and yours in the Hereafter," includes within its generality the prohibition of wearing silver, because the three mentioned together with it are unanimously forbidden to wear. And what is covered by the generality of an apparent text from the Book and the Sunnah may not be specified except by a text suitable for specification, as established in the science of the principles of jurisprudence (usul al-fiqh).

If it is said: The hadith is related regarding drinking from a silver vessel, not regarding wearing silver, the answer: The consideration is the generality of the wording, not the specificity of the occasion (sabab), especially since the Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned in the hadith what does not admit of any meaning other than wearing, such as silk and brocade.

If it is said: There has come in some authentic reports what explains this and clarifies that what is meant by silver is drinking from its vessels, not wearing it. Al-Bukhari said in his Sahih, "Chapter on drinking from gold vessels": Hafs ibn 'Umar narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from Ibn Abi Layla who said: "Hudhayfah was in al-Mada'in and he asked for water, and a dihqan brought him a cup of silver. He threw it at him and said: 'I did not throw it except that I had forbidden him, but he did not desist. The Prophet (ﷺ) forbade us from silk and brocade, and from drinking from vessels of gold and silver, and said: "They are theirs in this world and yours in the Hereafter."'" And "Chapter on silver vessels": Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Ibn 'Awn, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abi Layla, who said: "We went out with Hudhayfah," and he mentioned the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Do not drink from vessels of gold and silver, and do not wear silk and brocade, for they are theirs in this world (p. 357) and yours in the Hereafter." End of quote.

This detailed statement, which is the prohibition of drinking from vessels of gold and silver, and the prohibition of wearing silk and brocade, indicates that this is what is meant by the first report. In that case, there is no proof in the hadith for the prohibition of wearing silver, because it has been determined by these two reports that what is meant is drinking from its vessels, not wearing it, since the hadith is one single hadith.

The answer is in three aspects:

The first: The earlier report is general in its apparent meaning, covering both drinking and wearing together, while the reports restricted to drinking from its vessels without wearing mention some of the individual instances of the general term and are silent about others. It has been established in the principles of jurisprudence that "mentioning some individual instances of a general term under the ruling of the general term does not specify it." This is the correct view, as we have explained elsewhere. He alluded to it in Marāqi al-Su'ud (a versified work on the principles of jurisprudence) with his saying, joining what does not specify the general term according to the sound view:

"The mention of what agrees with it as a singular instance, and the view of the narrator upon the relied-upon position."

The second aspect: If that detailed statement were what the Prophet (ﷺ) intended, then gold would not be forbidden to wear, and only drinking from its vessels would be forbidden, just as the proponent of that distinction claimed regarding silver. This is because the reports containing that detailed statement say: "Do not drink from vessels of gold and silver," and their apparent meaning is that there is no difference between gold and silver. And wearing gold is unanimously forbidden for men.

The third aspect, which is the strongest, and one who has understood it correctly should not turn away from it because its meaning is clear, is this: The four mentioned in this hadith, which are gold, silver, silk, and brocade, the Prophet (ﷺ) explicitly stated that they belong to the disbelievers in this world and to the Muslims in the Hereafter. This indicates that whoever enjoys them in this world will not enjoy them in the Hereafter. Allah, Exalted and Most High, has stated in His Mighty Book that the people of Paradise enjoy gold and silver in two ways:

The first: drinking from their vessels.
The second: adorning themselves with them.

And He has made clear that the people of Paradise enjoy silk and brocade in one way only, which is wearing them, and the ruling on reclining on them falls under the ruling on wearing them. Thus the prohibition of gold and silver is established in both of the aforementioned ways, and the prohibition of silk and brocade in the one way, based on the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying, established in the authentic reports regarding the four mentioned: "They are theirs in this world, and yours in the Hereafter" (p. 358). For if enjoying silver were permitted in this world and the Hereafter, that would contradict his saying (ﷺ): "They are theirs in this world, and yours in the Hereafter." We will clarify this, Allah willing, from the Book of Allah, Exalted and Most High.

Know first: brocade (dibaj) is what is referred to in the Book of Allah as sundus and istabraq. Sundus is thin brocade, and istabraq is thick brocade.

Having known this, know that Allah, Exalted and Most High, explained the enjoyment of the people of Paradise in wearing gold and brocade, which is sundus and istabraq, in Surat al-Kahf, in His saying: ﴿Those, for them are Gardens of Eden, beneath which rivers flow. They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold, and they will wear green garments of fine silk and brocade﴾ [al-Kahf: 31]. So whoever wears gold and brocade in this world is deprived of this enjoyment of them mentioned in al-Kahf.

Exalted and Most High mentioned the enjoyment of the people of Paradise in wearing silk and gold in Surat al-Hajj, in His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds into gardens beneath which rivers flow. They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls, and their clothing therein will be silk﴾ [al-Hajj: 23–24].

He also explained their enjoyment of wearing gold and silk in Surat Fatir, in His saying: ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence, they will enter them. They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls, and their clothing therein will be silk. And they will say: "Praise be to Allah, who has removed from us the grief"﴾ [Fatir: 33–34]. So whoever wears gold and silk in this world is deprived of this enjoyment of them mentioned in Surat al-Hajj and Fatir.

He, Exalted and Most High, mentioned their enjoyment of wearing silk in Surat al-Insan, in His saying: ﴿And He will reward them for what they patiently endured with a garden and silk﴾ [al-Insan: 12], and in al-Dukhan with His saying: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in a secure place, within gardens and springs, wearing fine silk and brocade﴾ [al-Dukhan: 51–53]. So whoever wears silk in this world is deprived of this enjoyment of it mentioned in Surat al-Insan and al-Dukhan.

He, Exalted and Most High, mentioned their enjoyment of reclining on couches whose linings are "of istabraq" in Surat al-Rahman, in His saying: ﴿Reclining on beds whose linings are of istabraq﴾ [al-Rahman: 54]. So whoever reclines on brocade in this world is deprived of this enjoyment mentioned in Surat al-Rahman.

He, Exalted and Most High, also mentioned the enjoyment of the people of Paradise in wearing brocade, which is sundus and istabraq, and wearing silver (p. 359) in Surat al-Insan, in His saying: ﴿Upon them will be garments of fine green silk and brocade, and they will be adorned with bracelets of silver, and their Lord will give them a pure drink﴾ [al-Insan: 21].

So whoever wears brocade or silver in this world is deprived of enjoying their wearing mentioned in Surat al-Insan, because of the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "They are theirs in this world, and yours in the Hereafter." So if wearing silver were permitted in this world, together with His saying about the bliss of the people of Paradise: ﴿and they will be adorned with bracelets of silver﴾ [al-Insan: 21], that would contradict the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "They are theirs in this world, and yours in the Hereafter."

He mentioned the enjoyment of the people of Paradise in drinking from vessels of gold in Surat al-Zukhruf, in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿They will be served with platters of gold and cups﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 71]. So whoever drinks from gold vessels in this world is deprived of this enjoyment of them mentioned in al-Zukhruf.

He, Exalted and Most High, mentioned the enjoyment of the people of Paradise in drinking from vessels of silver in Surat al-Insan, in His saying: ﴿And there will be circulated among them vessels of silver and cups of crystal, crystal of silver, which they have determined in measure. And they will be given to drink therein a cup whose mixture is of ginger, from a spring therein named Salsabil﴾ [al-Insan: 15–18]. So whoever drinks from silver vessels in this world is deprived of this enjoyment of them mentioned in Surat al-Insan.

Thus it has become clear through this exposition the indication of the Qur'an and the authentic Sunnah on the prohibition of wearing silver. And knowledge is with Allah, Exalted and Most High.

* *

Clarification (tanbih).

If it is said: The generality of the aforementioned hadith of Hudhayfah, which you cited as evidence, and the explanation of the Qur'an, that it includes wearing silver and drinking from it, and you said that its being related regarding drinking from silver vessels does not make it specific to that. So what is the evidence for this, that the consideration is the generality of the wording and not the specificity of the occasion (sabab)?

Al-Bukhari said in his Sahih: Musaddad narrated to us, Yazid ibn Zurai' narrated to us, Sulayman al-Taymi narrated to us, from Abu 'Uthman, from Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him): "A man had kissed a woman, so he came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and mentioned that to him, and there was revealed to him: ﴿And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and in the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with bad deeds. That is a reminder for those who remember [Allah]﴾ [Hud: 114]. The man said: 'Is this for me?' He said: 'For whoever acts upon it from my ummah.'" End of quote. This is the wording of al-Bukhari in the tafsir section on Surat Hud. In another narration in the Sahih, he said: "For all of my ummah, all of them." End of quote.

So this man who kissed the woman had a verse revealed concerning his particular case, a verse whose wording is general, and he asked the Prophet (ﷺ): "Is this for me?" The meaning of that is: is the text specific to me because I was the cause of its revelation, or is it upon the generality of its wording? The Prophet's (ﷺ) saying "For all of my ummah" means that the consideration is the generality of the wording: ﴿Indeed, good deeds do away with bad deeds﴾, not the specificity of the occasion (sabab). And knowledge is with Allah, exalted.

As for His saying, glorified and exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿And you see the ships﴾ [al-Nahl: 14], i.e., the ships (al-fulk). The Qur'an has shown that "al-fulk" is applied to the singular and to the plural, and that when it is applied to the singular it is masculine, and when applied to the plural it is feminine. He applied it to the singular in masculine form in His saying: ﴿And a sign for them is that We carried their offspring in the laden ship, and We created for them of its likeness that which they ride﴾ [Ya-Sin: 41-42]. He applied it to the plural in feminine form in His saying: ﴿And the ships which run in the sea with that which benefits people﴾ [al-Baqarah: 164], and His saying: ﴿mawakhir﴾ [al-Nahl: 14], which is the plural of makhirah, an active participle. "Makhirat al-safinah yamkhuru" (with fatha) and "yamkhuru" (with damma) — makhran and mukhuran: the ship went through the sea cutting the water with a sound. It is also said: it faced the wind in its course. The more apparent view regarding His saying: ﴿And that you may seek of His bounty﴾ [al-Nahl: 14] is that it is coordinated (ma'tuf) upon His saying: ﴿that you may eat from it fresh meat﴾ [al-Nahl: 14], and perhaps "la'alla" here indicates purpose (ta'lil), as has been mentioned previously.

Gratitude (shukr) in the Shari'ah: it is used of the servant towards his Lord, as in His saying here: ﴿so that you may be grateful﴾ [al-Nahl: 14]. The servant's gratitude to his Lord is his employing the blessings which He has bestowed upon him in His obedience. As for one who seeks help with Allah's blessings in disobeying Him, he is not among the grateful; rather he is ungrateful and disbelieving (kanud kafur).

As for the gratitude of the Lord toward His servant, mentioned in the Qur'an, such as His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Shakir, All-Knowing﴾ [al-Baqarah: 158], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving, Shakur﴾ [Fatir: 34], it means that He rewards His servant with a generous reward for a small deed. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 15:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He cast into the earth firm mountains lest it should shake with you, and rivers and roads, that you may be guided, and landmarks; and by the star they are guided﴾. In these two verses He, exalted and mighty is He, mentioned four of His blessings upon His creation, making clear to them the magnitude of His favour upon them through them:

The first: His casting of the mountains into the earth so that it would be steady and not move. He repeated the reminder of this blessing in the Qur'an,

• like His saying: ﴿Have We not made the earth a resting-place, and the mountains as stakes?﴾ [al-Naba': 6-7],

• and His saying: ﴿And We placed in the earth firm mountains﴾ [al-Anbiya': 31] – the verse in full,

• and His saying: ﴿And We placed in it firm mountains, lofty ones﴾ [al-Mursalat: 27],

• and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He created the heavens without pillars that you see, and cast into the earth firm mountains lest it should shake with you﴾ [Luqman: 10] – the verse in full,

• and His saying: ﴿And the mountains He has set firm﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 32],

and the verses of this kind are very many.

The meaning of tamid (تَمِيدُ) is: it would incline and be agitated.

Regarding the meaning of His saying "an" (أنْ), there are two well-known opinions among the scholars: the first is "lest it incline with you" (كَراهَةُ أنْ تَمِيدَ بِكم, i.e., out of dislike that it should incline with you). The second is that the meaning is: "so that it does not incline with you" (لِئَلّا تَمِيدَ بِكم). Both are close in meaning.

The second: His making the rivers flow in the earth, mentioned here in His saying: "and rivers" [al-Nahl: 15]. In the Qur'an He, exalted is He, repeated the reminder of His causing water to gush forth in the earth for His creation:

• like His saying: ﴿And He subjected for you the rivers, and subjected for you the sun and the moon﴾ – the verse in full [Ibrahim: 32-33],

• and His saying: ﴿Have you considered the water which you drink? Did you bring it down from the cloud, or are We the sender? Had We willed, We would have made it bitter; so why do you not give thanks?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 68-70],

• and His saying: ﴿And We caused springs to gush forth in it, that they may eat of its fruit﴾ – the verse in full [Ya-Sin: 34-35],

along with other verses.

The third: His making roads in the earth which people traverse, travelling in them from region to region seeking their needs, mentioned here in His saying: "and roads" (وسُبُلًا). It is the plural of sabil (سَبِيلٍ), meaning "path". He repeated the reminder of this in the Qur'an:

• like His saying: ﴿And We made in it broad roads, that they may be guided﴾ [al-Anbiya': 31],

• and His saying: ﴿And Allah has made the earth a spread-out carpet for you, that you may traverse therein broad roads﴾ [Nuh: 19],

• and His saying: ﴿He said: "Its knowledge is with my Lord in a Book; my Lord neither errs nor forgets — the One who made the earth a cradle for you and threaded for you therein roads"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 52-53].

And His saying: ﴿It is He who made the earth subservient to you, so walk in its broad tracts﴾ – the verse in full [al-Mulk: 15], and His saying: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "The Mighty, the All-Knowing created them, who made the earth a cradle for you and made for you therein roads, that you may be guided"﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 9-10], along with other verses.

The fourth: His making landmarks for the children of Adam, that they might be guided by them in the darknesses of land and sea, mentioned here in His saying: ﴿and landmarks; and by the star they are guided﴾ [al-Nahl: 16]. The reminder of something similar has been mentioned in the Qur'an in His saying: ﴿And it is He who made for you the stars, that you may be guided by them in the darknesses of land and sea﴾ – the verse in full [al-An'am: 97].

Al-Shinqiti's words on the verse: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Is then He who creates like one who does not create?﴾ and the rest of the verse. The explanation of this verse has already preceded in two places.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 18:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if you should count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate it. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. In this noble verse, He - exalted is He and high is He - mentioned that the children of Adam are unable to enumerate the favors of Allah because of their abundance upon them, and He followed that with His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [an-Nahl: 18]. This indicates the shortcoming of the children of Adam in thanking those favors, and that Allah forgives those among them who repent, and forgives whomever He wills for that shortcoming in thanking the favors. He clarified this implied meaning referred to here by His saying: ﴿And if you should count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate it. Indeed, mankind is ever a wrongdoer and ungrateful﴾ [Ibrahim: 34].

He clarified in another place that all the favors upon the children of Adam are from Him - exalted is He and high is He - and that is in His saying: ﴿And whatever favor you have is from Allah﴾ [an-Nahl: 53], and so on.

In this noble verse there is evidence that the singular noun, when it is a generic noun (ism jins) and is annexed (idafa) to a definite noun, is general (ya'ummu), as is established in the principles of jurisprudence (al-Usul, i.e. usul al-fiqh). For ﴿the favor of Allah﴾ [an-Nahl: 18] is a singular noun annexed to a definite noun, so it encompasses all favors. To this is the allusion in the saying of the author of Maraqi as-Su'ud, listing it among the forms of generality:

"Or by annexation to a definite noun, when specification is established it is negated."

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 24:**

His saying, Most High: ﴿When it is said to them, "What has your Lord sent down?" they say, "Fables of the ancients."﴾ In this noble verse, He, Glorified and Exalted, mentions that when the disbelievers are asked about what Allah sent down to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), they say: "Nothing has been sent down to him. What he speaks is only fables of the ancients, which he has copied from their books." *Asatir* (fables, myths) is the plural of *ustura* or *istara*, and it means what is written in the books of the earlier people, of falsehoods and vanities. Its root is from *satara*, meaning "he wrote." From this is His saying, Most High: ﴿and a written Book﴾ [al-Tur: 2]. Some scholars said: *asatir* means trivialities and vanities. This meaning is clarified in other verses, such as His saying: ﴿And they say, "Fables of the ancients, which he has had written down, and they are dictated to him morning and evening."﴾ [al-Furqan: 5], and His saying: ﴿And when Our verses are recited to them, they say, "We have heard. If we wished, we could say the like of this. This is nothing but fables of the ancients."﴾ [al-Anfal: 31], along with other verses.

His saying *"mada"* (what): it is possible that *dha* is a relative pronoun (*mawsula*) and *ma* is the subject (*mubtada'*), and the clause *"unzila"* (was sent down) is the relative clause, and the relative pronoun with its clause is the predicate of the subject. It is also possible that the two together form a single noun in the accusative position, as the object of *anzala* (sent down). This is what he indicated in the *Khulasa* (Alfiyya) with his saying:

> "And the like of *madha* after an interrogative, or *man*, when it is not nullified in the speech."

Glorified and Exalted, He showed the falsehood of the disbelievers' claim that the Qur'an is "fables of the ancients" in His saying: ﴿Say: "It was sent down by the One who knows the secret [of the heavens and the earth]"﴾ [al-Furqan: 6], and by His saying here: ﴿so that they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [al-Nahl: 25].

(p-363)

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 25:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and of the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge. Unquestionably evil is that which they bear.﴾ In this noble verse, He - exalted and majestic - mentions that those disbelievers who turn people away from the Qur'an by claiming that it is "the fables of the ancients" bear their burdens - that is, their sins - in full, and [also bear] some of the burdens of their followers who followed them into misguidance; as indicated by the particle of partition, which is "wa-min" (and of), in His saying: ﴿and of the burdens of those whom they mislead﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Nahl: 25].

Al-Qurtubi said: "min" (of) is for specifying the kind; so they bear the like of the burdens of those whom they misled, in full.

And He, exalted, clarified this meaning in His saying: ﴿And they will surely bear their own burdens and additional burdens along with their burdens. And they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to invent﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 13]. The lam in His saying "li-yahmilu" (that they may bear) is connected to an omitted element that the context indicates, meaning: We decreed for them that they would say about the Qur'an, "fables of the ancients," so that they might bear their burdens.

Caution.

If it is said: What is the manner of their bearing some of the burdens of others, which is stated in His saying: ﴿and of the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Nahl: 25], and His saying: ﴿And they will surely bear their own burdens and additional burdens along with their burdens﴾ to the end of the verse [al-'Ankabut: 13], given that Allah says: ﴿And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾ [Fatir: 18], and He, exalted and majestic, says: ﴿And no soul earns [blame] except against itself﴾ [al-An'am: 164], and says: ﴿That is a nation that has passed on. For it is what it earned, and for you is what you earned. And you will not be questioned about what they used to do﴾ [al-Baqarah: 134, 141], and other verses?

The answer - and Allah knows best - is that the leaders of misguidance and their chiefs bore two burdens: One of them: the burden of their own misguidance. And the second: the burden of their misleading others; because whoever establishes an evil practice bears its burden and the burden of whoever acts upon it, and that does not diminish anything from their burdens. He is taken to account for the action of others only because he is the one who initiated it and caused it, so he is punished for it from this aspect, since it is from his own doing. Thus it is not contrary to His saying: ﴿And no bearer of burdens will bear [the burden] of another﴾ to the end of the verse [Fatir: 18].

Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj - may Allah have mercy on him - said in his Sahih: "Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me, Jarir ibn 'Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Musa ibn 'Abdullah ibn Yazid, and Abu al-Duha, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Hilal al-'Absi, from Jarir ibn 'Abdullah, who said: 'Some people from the Bedouins came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wearing woolen garments. He saw their poor condition, for they had been struck by need, so he urged the people to give charity. They were slow to respond to him, until that was seen in his face.' He said: 'Then a man from the Ansar came with a purse of silver, then another came, and then they followed one another until the joy was recognized in his face. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever establishes a good practice in Islam, and it is acted upon after him, there will be written for him the like of the reward of whoever acts upon it, and nothing will be diminished from their rewards. And whoever establishes an evil practice in Islam, and it is acted upon after him, there will be written against him the like of the burden of whoever acts upon it, and nothing will be diminished from their burdens."'" End of quotation.

Muslim recorded this hadith in his Sahih from Jarir ibn 'Abdullah through multiple chains. He also recorded something similar from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah with the wording: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever calls to guidance will have a reward like the rewards of those who follow him, nothing being diminished from their rewards. And whoever calls to misguidance will bear a sin like the sins of those who follow him, nothing being diminished from their sins." End of quotation.

The compiler, may Allah pardon him, says: These authentic texts indicate the resolution of the apparent difficulty between the verses, just as they indicate that all the good deeds of this Ummah are in the record of the Prophet ﷺ, so he has the like of the rewards of all of them, because he - may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him - is the one who established for them all the good practices in Islam. We ask Allah to grant him the intercession and the lofty rank, and to send blessings and peace upon him in the most complete manner and the purest greeting.

His saying in this noble verse: ﴿without knowledge﴾ [al-Nahl: 25], indicates that the disbeliever is not excused after the messengers have conveyed the message, supported by miracles, in which there is no confusion regarding the truth, even if he thinks that his disbelief is guidance; for what prevented him from recognizing the truth despite its manifestness was nothing but intense partisanship for disbelief, as we mentioned the verses that indicate this in "al-A'raf"; such as His saying: ﴿Indeed, they took the devils as allies besides Allah, and they think that they are guided﴾ [al-A'raf: 30], and His saying: ﴿Say: Shall we inform you of the greatest losers in deeds? Those whose effort is lost in the worldly life while they think that they are doing well in work﴾ [al-Kahf: 103-104], and His saying: ﴿And there will appear to them from Allah that which they had not been counting on﴾ [al-Zumar: 47]. Their bearing of their burdens is their acquiring of sin, which is the cause of their falling into the Fire - may Allah protect us and the Muslims from it.

Some scholars said: The meaning of their bearing their burdens is that each one of them, upon emerging from his grave on the Day of Resurrection, will be met by something in the most ugly form and the most foul smell; so he says: "Who are you?" It says: "Do you not recognize me?" He says: "No, by Allah, except that Allah has made your face ugly and your smell foul!" It says: "I am your evil deed. In the worldly life you were of evil deed and foul; how often you rode me in the world! Come, let me ride you today." So he rides on its back. End of quotation.

His saying ﴿Unquestionably evil is that which they bear﴾ [al-Nahl: 25]: "sa'a" (evil is) is an invariable verb used to express blame, with the meaning of "bi'sa" (wretched is). And "ma" in it has the two possibilities referred to in his saying in the Khulasah:

"Ma is a distinguisher; and it is said to be a subject, in such as 'na'am' (yes), says the excellent one."

His saying "yazirun," i.e., they bear. Qatadah said: they do. End of quotation.

⁕ ⁕ ⁕

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Nahl.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and of the burdens of those whom they mislead﴾ to the end of the verse.

This noble verse indicates that these misguided ones bear their burdens in full, and also bear some of the burdens of the followers whom they misled.

Other verses have come indicating that no one bears the burden of another, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if one heavily laden calls [another] to [carry] his load, nothing of it will be carried, even if he should be a close relative﴾ [Fatir: 18], and His saying: ﴿And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾ [al-An'am: 164].

The answer is that these misguided ones bore only their own burdens, for they bore the burden of misguidance and the burden of misleading others.

For whoever establishes an evil practice, upon him is its burden, and the burden of whoever acts upon it; this does not diminish anything from their burdens, because his instituting it for others is a sin among his sins, so he is taken to account for it.

By this the difficulty also disappears in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they will surely bear their own burdens and additional burdens along with their burdens﴾ to the end of the verse [al-'Ankabut: 13].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 26:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Those before them had already plotted﴾.

In this noble verse, Allah, Majestic and Exalted, mentions that the disbelievers who lived before the disbelievers of Makkah had indeed plotted. He clarified this in other places, such as His saying: ﴿And those before them had already plotted, but to Allah belongs all plotting﴾ [al-Ra'd: 42], and His saying: ﴿And they have plotted their plot, but with Allah is their plot, though their plot would have moved mountains﴾ [Ibrahim: 46].

He clarified some of the plotting of the disbelievers of Makkah in His saying: ﴿And [recall] when those who disbelieved plotted against you to restrain you or kill you or expel you﴾ (the verse) [al-Anfal: 30].

He mentioned some of the plotting of the Jews in His saying: ﴿And they plotted, and Allah plotted, and Allah is the best of plotters﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 54].

He clarified some of the plotting of the people of Salih in His saying: ﴿And they plotted a plot, and We plotted a plot while they perceived not. So see how was the outcome of their plot: that We destroyed them and their people entirely﴾ (the verses) [al-Naml: 50-51].

He mentioned some of the plotting of the people of Nuh in His saying: ﴿And they plotted a great plot, and said, "Do not leave your gods"﴾ (the verse) [Nuh: 22-23].

He clarified the plotting of the leaders of the disbelievers in His saying: ﴿Rather, the plotting of the night and day, when you commanded us to disbelieve in Allah﴾ (the verse) [Saba': 33]. Al-Makr (plotting, lit. "deception") is the display of what is good while concealing what is evil, and it is deceit. Allah, Majestic and Exalted, has clarified that the harm of evil plotting returns only upon its doer, in His saying: ﴿And evil plotting does not encompass except its own people﴾ [Fatir: 43].

* *

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿So Allah came at their structure from the foundations﴾. That is, He uprooted it from its base and pulled it out from its foundation, so He nullified their work and brought down their structure. What was done to these disbelievers, namely Nimrod and his people, as we mentioned in "Surat al-Hijr," He also did similarly to other disbelievers. He nullified what they were doing and planning, as in His saying: ﴿And We destroyed what Pharaoh and his people were making and what they were building up﴾ [al-A'raf: 137], and His saying: ﴿Every time they kindle a fire for war, Allah extinguishes it﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 64], and His saying: ﴿So Allah came at them from where they did not expect, and He cast terror into their hearts; they destroyed their houses by their own hands and the hands of the believers. So take warning, O you with insight﴾ [al-Hashr: 2], along with other verses.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 27:**

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then on the Day of Resurrection He will disgrace them﴾, meaning: He will expose them before all witnesses and humiliate them by revealing their disgraces and what their hearts concealed, making it public.

He clarified this meaning in other places, such as His saying: ﴿Does he not know that when what is in the graves is scattered out and what is within the breasts is obtained?﴾ [al-'Adiyat: 9-10], meaning: He brings into the open what the breasts used to conceal. And His saying: ﴿The Day when secrets are examined﴾ [al-Tariq: 9].

Exalted and Majestic is He, has also made clear in another place that whoever is made to enter the Fire has indeed received this disgrace mentioned, in His saying: ﴿Our Lord, indeed whoever You admit to the Fire, You have disgraced him﴾ [Al 'Imran: 192]. We have already explained the meaning of *khizy* (disgrace) in Surah Hud.

* *

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And He will say, "Where are My partners, those you used to dispute about?"﴾. In this noble verse, Exalted and Majestic is He, mentions that He will question the polytheists on the Day of Resurrection with a question of rebuke. He will say to them: where are the objects of worship about which you used to contend with My messengers and their followers, saying that you must necessarily associate them with Me in My worship?

He explained this meaning in other places, such as:

- His saying: ﴿And the Day He calls to them and says, "Where are My partners whom you used to claim?"﴾ [al-Qasas: 62, 74].
- His saying: ﴿And it will be said to them, "Where is that which you used to worship besides Allah? Can they help you or defend themselves?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 92-93].
- His saying: ﴿Then it will be said to them, "Where is that which you used to associate besides Allah?" They will say, "They have gone astray from us"﴾ to the end of the verse [Ghafir: 73-74].
- His saying: ﴿Until, when Our messengers come to them to take them in death, they will say, "Where is that which you used to invoke besides Allah?" They will say, "They have gone astray from us"﴾ to the end of the verse [al-A'raf: 37].

and other verses besides these.

The majority of reciters read *shurakai* (﴿شُرَكائِيَ﴾) [al-Nahl: 27] with a hamzah and the first person pronoun ya'. Ibn Kathir, through the transmission of al-Bazzi, is reported to have read *shurakaya* (﴿شُرَكايَ﴾) with the first person ya' without a hamzah, but this reading is not established.

The majority read *tushaqqun* (﴿تُشاقُّونَ﴾) [al-Nahl: 27] with a fatha-vowelled nun of the verb (the nun of raf', indicative marker), with the object omitted.

Nafi' read *tushaqqunni* (﴿تُشاقُّونِ﴾) with a kasra on the light nun, which is the nun of protection (*nun al-wiqayah*), with the object being the first person pronoun ya', indicated by the kasra, while the nun of raf' is dropped. This is permissible, because it may be dropped without any governing or jussive particle when it is combined with the nun of protection, as already explained in Surah al-Hijr, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿So by what [means] do you give me good tidings?﴾ [al-Hijr: 54].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 28:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So they will offer submission﴾, i.e., submission (al-istislam) and humility (al-khudu'). The meaning is: they will show complete obedience and submission, and abandon the opposition in which they used to be. This happens when they witness death, or on the Day of Resurrection. That is to say: in this world they oppose the Messengers, i.e., they contradict and oppose them, but when they witness the reality they "offer submission," i.e., they humble themselves, surrender and submit, at a time when that does them no good.

Among what the Qur'an indicates that the meaning of "offering submission" (ilqa' al-salam) is humility and surrender is His saying: ﴿And do not say to one who gives you [a greeting of] peace, "You are not a believer"﴾ [an-Nisa': 94], according to the reading of Nafi', Ibn 'Amir and Hamzah without an alif after the lam, in the sense of submission and compliance. And His saying: ﴿But if they withdraw from you and do not fight you and offer you peace (al-salam)﴾, the verse [an-Nisa': 91].

The view that al-salam in the last two verses means reconciliation and truce does not contradict what we have mentioned, because the one who makes peace is submissive and compliant with what he has agreed to of abandoning evil. And His saying: ﴿And they will offer submission to Allah that Day, and lost from them is what they used to fabricate﴾ [an-Nahl: 87], all of it carries the meaning of surrender, humility and compliance. Compliance at the witnessing of death does not benefit, as we have stated, and as many verses indicate, such as His saying: ﴿And repentance is not [accepted] from those who continue to do evil deeds until, when death comes to one of them, he says, "Indeed, I have repented now"﴾ [an-Nisa': 18], and His saying: ﴿But their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our punishment﴾ [Ghafir: 85] (p-368), and His saying: ﴿Now? And you had disobeyed before and were among the corrupters﴾ [Yunus: 91], and other verses.

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿We did not used to do any evil. Yes! Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what you used to do﴾, meaning that those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves, when they witness the reality, will offer submission and say: ﴿We did not used to do any evil﴾ [an-Nahl: 28]. His saying ﴿We did not used to do any evil﴾ is the object of an omitted verb of saying, without disagreement.

The meaning is that they deny the evil they used to do, namely disbelief, denying the Messengers, and sins. Allah has shown their lie by His saying: ﴿Yes! Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what you used to do﴾ [an-Nahl: 28].

He has explained in other places that they deny the disbelief and sins they were upon, as mentioned here, and He has also shown their lie in that, such as:

• His saying: ﴿Then their discourse will not be but that they will say, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists." Look how they have lied against themselves, and lost from them is what they used to fabricate﴾ [al-An'am: 23-24],

• And His saying: ﴿They will say, "They have strayed from us; rather, we had not been calling upon anything before." Thus does Allah leave astray﴾ [Ghafir: 74],

• And His saying: ﴿On the Day Allah will resurrect them all and they will swear to Him as they swear to you, and they think they are upon something. Unquestionably, they are the liars﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 18],

• And His saying: ﴿And they will say, "A forbidden ban"﴾ [al-Furqan: 22],

i.e., a forbidden prohibition that you should touch us with evil, because we did not do what would make us deserve that; and other verses.

His saying here: "Yes" [an-Nahl: 28] is a refutation of them in their saying: ﴿We did not used to do any evil﴾.

Note.

The word "Yes" (bala) in the Arabic language comes only for one of two meanings, with no third:

The first: that it comes to annul a preceding negation in the speech. It is thus the opposite of "no" (la), because "la" negates affirmation, and "bala" negates negation, such as His saying here: ﴿We did not used to do any evil﴾ [an-Nahl: 28]; this negation has been negated by the word "bala", i.e., you used to do evil of disbelief and sins; and such as His saying: ﴿Those who disbelieve claim that they will never be resurrected. Say, "Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected"﴾ [at-Taghabun: 7]; and His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "The Hour will not come to us." Say, "Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come to you"﴾ [Saba': 3]; and His saying: ﴿And they say, "None will enter Paradise except one who is a Jew or a Christian"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 111] (p-369), for He negated this negation with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Yes, whoever submits his face to Allah﴾, the verse [al-Baqarah: 112]. Similar to this is much in the Qur'an and in the speech of the Arabs.

The second: that it is an answer to a question accompanied specifically by a negation;

• such as His saying: ﴿Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes"﴾ [al-A'raf: 172],

• and His saying: ﴿Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them? Yes﴾ [Ya-Sin: 81],

• and His saying: ﴿Did there not come to you your messengers with clear evidence?" They said, "Yes"﴾ [Ghafir: 50],

This also is common in the Qur'an and in the speech of the Arabs. As for when the question is not accompanied by a negation, its answer is with "na'am" (yes), not "bala". The answer to a negated question with "na'am" is attested but not analogical, such as his saying:

Did not the night gather Umm 'Amr and us? So that is what brings us close, yes.

And you see the crescent as I see it, and the day rises over it as it rose over me.

So the proper place here is for "bala", not for "na'am", in this verse.

If it is said: These verses indicate that the disbelievers will conceal on the Day of Resurrection what they were upon of disbelief and sins, as His saying about them: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ [al-An'am: 23], and His saying: ﴿We did not used to do any evil﴾ [an-Nahl: 28], and the like. Yet Allah has stated explicitly that they will not conceal any statement, in His saying: ﴿And they will not conceal from Allah any statement﴾ [an-Nisa': 42].

The answer is what we have mentioned before: that they say with their tongues, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists"; then Allah seals their mouths, and their hands and feet speak of what they used to earn. So the concealment is with respect to speaking the denial with the tongues, and the non-concealment is with respect to the testimony of their limbs against them. And Allah the Exalted knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 29:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So enter the gates of Hell﴾ and so on. Here He did not specify the number of its gates, but He did specify it in "Surat al-Hijr" in His saying, majestic and exalted is He: ﴿It has seven gates; for each gate there is an allotted portion [of them]﴾ [al-Hijr: 44]. I ask Allah to protect us and our Muslim brothers from it and from all of its gates; indeed He is Merciful and Generous.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 30:**

Allah's saying: ﴿And it will be said to those who were mindful of Allah: "What has your Lord sent down?" They will say: "Good."﴾ In this noble verse, Allah, Mighty and Exalted, mentions that when the God-fearing (al-muttaqun) are asked about what Allah sent down to His Messenger (ﷺ), they say: "He sent down good to him," meaning mercy, guidance and blessing for whoever follows him and believes in him. What is understood from the description of the people of this answer, as being God-fearing, is that those who are not God-fearing give a different answer. Allah has explicitly stated this implication in His saying about those who are not God-fearing, namely the disbelievers: ﴿And when it is said to them, "What has your Lord sent down?" they say, "Tales of the ancients."﴾ [al-Nahl: 24], as has already been mentioned.

* *

Allah's saying: ﴿For those who did good in this world, there is good.﴾ In this noble verse, Allah, Mighty and Exalted, mentions that whoever does good in this abode, which is the world (al-dunya), will have with Allah a good recompense in the Hereafter. He clarified this meaning in many verses:

• Such as His saying: ﴿For those who did good is the best (al-husna) and more (ziyada). Neither darkness nor humiliation will cover their faces﴾ to the end of the verse [Yunus: 26]. Al-husna is Paradise, and al-ziyada is looking upon the Noble Face of Allah.

• And His saying: ﴿And He will reward those who did good with the best﴾ [al-Najm: 31].

• And His saying: ﴿Is the recompense for good anything but good?﴾ [al-Rahman: 60].

• And His saying: ﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have better than it﴾ [al-Qasas: 84].

His saying in this verse, ḥasana (good), means a good recompense, namely Paradise and its bliss. The verses of this kind are numerous.

* *

Allah's saying: ﴿And the abode of the Hereafter is better.﴾ In this noble verse, Allah, Mighty and Exalted, mentions that the abode of the Hereafter is better than the abode of the world. He repeated this meaning in many places,

• such as His saying: ﴿And those who were given knowledge said, "Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better"﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Qasas: 80],

• and His saying: ﴿And what is with Allah is better for the righteous﴾,

• and His saying: ﴿But you prefer the worldly life, while the Hereafter is better and more lasting﴾,

• and His saying: ﴿And the Hereafter is better for you than the first﴾ [al-Duha: 4],

• and His saying: ﴿Beautified for people is the love of desires: women, children, heaped-up piles of gold and silver, branded horses, livestock and tilled land. That is the enjoyment of the worldly life, but Allah has the best return. Say: "Shall I inform you of something better than that? For those who are mindful of Allah are gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein, and purified spouses, and approval from Allah"﴾ to the end of the verse [Al 'Imran: 14–15], and His saying, khayr (better) [al-Nahl: 30].

Khayr is a comparative form (sigha tafdil) whose hamza has been dropped because of its frequent use, for lightness.

Ibn Malik alluded to this in his al-Kafiya (a grammatical work, "The Sufficient") with his saying:

*Often they dispensed with "khayr" and "sharr" (good and evil) with respect to their saying "akhyar minhu" and "ashar" (better than it, worse than it).*

The abode was called "the Last Abode" (al-dar al-akhira) because it is the final dwelling place, so there is no transfer from it at all to another abode.

Before reaching it, a person moves from one place to another. His beginning is from dust. Then he moved from the origin of dust to the origin of a drop of semen, then to a clinging clot, then to a lump of flesh, then to bones. Then (p-371) Allah clothed the bones with flesh, produced him as another creation, brought him out into the world in this abode, then he moves to the grave, then to the place of gathering, then they disperse: ﴿On that Day people will come forth in scattered groups﴾ [al-Zalzala: 6]. Some go to the right toward Paradise, and some go to the left toward the Fire: ﴿And on the Day the Hour is established, on that Day they will be divided. As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, they will be in a meadow, made joyful. And as for those who disbelieved and denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter, those will be brought forward to punishment﴾ [al-Rum: 14–16].

When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of the Fire enter the Fire, then the staff of the one who is fleeing (al-tasyar) will be cast down, death will be slaughtered, and it will be said: "O people of Paradise, eternity, there is no death! O people of the Fire, eternity, there is no death!" That will remain forever, with no cessation and no transfer from it to another place.

This is the meaning of describing it as "the Hereafter," as Allah, Mighty and Exalted, clarified by His saying: ﴿And We created man from an extract of clay. Then We made him a drop in a firm place. Then We made the drop into a clinging clot, then We made the clot into a lump, then We made the lump into bones, then We clothed the bones with flesh. Then We produced him as another creation. So blessed is Allah, the best of creators. Then indeed, after that, you will surely die. Then indeed, on the Day of Resurrection, you will be raised﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 12–16].

Note.

In this noble verse, Allah, Mighty and Exalted, added "the abode" (al-dar) to "the Hereafter" (al-akhira), although the abode is the Hereafter, as shown by His saying: ﴿And the abode of the Hereafter﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Nahl: 30], by the definiteness of "the abode" and describing it as "the Hereafter" elsewhere. In accordance with what Ibn Malik said in al-Khulasa (his versified summary of grammar, "The Essence"):

*A noun is not annexed to what is identical to it in meaning, and interpret it if the form causes confusion.*

So the word "al-dar" is interpreted as referring to the name of the Hereafter. We explained in our book (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab, "Removing the Appearance of Inconsistency from the Verses of the Book") in "Surat Fatir," in discussing His saying: "and the evil plotting" [Fatir: 43], that what appears to us is that the annexation of a thing to itself with two different words is a style of the Arabic language, for treating difference in wording as difference in meaning. We explained how common it is in the Qur'an and in Arabic speech. And knowledge is with Allah, Exalted.

* *

Allah's saying: ﴿And how excellent is the abode of the God-fearing.﴾ Allah, Mighty and Exalted, praised the abode of the God-fearing, which is Paradise, in this noble verse, because ni'ma (how excellent), is a rigid verb (fi'l jamid) used to express praise. He repeated His commendation of it in many verses, because in it is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. As (p-372) Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for their eyes﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Sajda: 17], and He said: ﴿And when you look there, you will see bliss and a great dominion﴾ [al-Insan: 20]. The verses of this kind are very numerous.

He - may He be exalted and glorified - mentions in this noble verse that the God-fearing will enter the Gardens of Eden (*'adn*) on the Day of Resurrection. In the language of the Arabs, *'adn* means residence. So the meaning of "Gardens of Eden" is gardens of lasting residence in bliss, from which they will not depart or seek to move.

He has made clear in many verses that they will remain in Paradise forever, as He indicated here by the word *'adn*. Examples include:

• His saying: ﴿They will not desire any change from it﴾ [al-Kahf: 108].

• His saying: ﴿He who has settled us in the abode of residence by His bounty﴾ [Fatir: 35]. *Al-muqamah* means residence. It is established in *tasrif* (morphology) that when a verb has more than three letters, its mimi verbal noun (*al-masdar al-mimi*), its noun of time, and its noun of place are all in the form of the passive participle (*ism al-maf'ul*).

• His saying: ﴿Indeed, the God-fearing will be in a secure station﴾ [al-Dukhan: 51], according to the reading of Nafi' and Ibn Amir, with the *mim* vowelled with a *damma* from *al-iqamah* (residence).

• His saying: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a good reward, remaining in it forever﴾ [al-Kahf: 2-3].

And other verses besides these.

His saying in this noble verse: ﴿Rivers flow beneath them﴾ [al-Nahl: 31].

He explained the kinds of those rivers in His saying: ﴿Therein are rivers of water unaltered, and rivers of milk whose taste does not change, and rivers of wine delicious to drinkers, and rivers of purified honey﴾ [Muhammad: 15]. His saying here: ﴿They will have therein whatever they wish﴾ [al-Nahl: 31] He clarified in other places, such as:

• His saying: ﴿They will have whatever they wish therein, and with Us is more﴾ [Qaf: 35].

• His saying: ﴿And therein is whatever the souls desire and whatever the eyes delight in, and you will abide therein eternally﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 71].

• His saying: ﴿They will have therein whatever they wish, abiding eternally. That is ever upon your Lord a promise that is due﴾ [al-Furqan: 16].

• His saying: ﴿They will have whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the reward of the good-doers﴾ [al-Zumar: 34].

• His saying: ﴿And for you therein is whatever your souls desire, and for you therein is whatever you request as a welcome from the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ [Fussilat: 31-32].

And other verses besides these.

His saying in this verse: ﴿Thus does Allah reward the God-fearing﴾ [al-Nahl: 31].

This indicates that the fear of Allah (*taqwa*) is the cause by which Paradise is attained.

He, exalted is He, has also clarified this meaning in other places, such as:

• His saying: ﴿That is the Paradise which We cause to inherit to those of Our servants who were God-fearing﴾ [Maryam: 63].

• His saying: ﴿And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden whose width is the heavens and the earth, prepared for the God-fearing﴾ [Al 'Imran: 133].

• His saying: ﴿Indeed, the God-fearing will be in gardens and springs﴾ (p-373) [al-Hijr: 45].

• His saying: ﴿Indeed, the God-fearing will be within gardens and bliss﴾ [al-Tur: 17].

And other verses besides these.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 32:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those whom the angels take in death while they are good, saying, "Peace be upon you; enter Paradise for what you used to do."﴾ In this noble verse, He - exalted and majestic is He - mentions that the God-fearing (al-muttaqin), who used to comply with the commands of their Lord and avoid His prohibitions, are taken in death by the angels; that is, the angels seize their souls while they are in the state of being good (tayyibin), meaning pure from polytheism and sins, according to the most correct interpretations, and they give them the good news of Paradise and greet them with peace.

This meaning is also explained in other places, such as:

• His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast - the angels descend upon them, [saying], "Do not fear and do not grieve, but receive good news of Paradise, which you were promised."﴾ [Fussilat: 30],

• and His saying: ﴿And its keepers will say to them, "Peace be upon you; you have been good, so enter it, abiding eternally."﴾ [al-Zumar: 73],

• and His saying: ﴿The angels will enter upon them from every gate, [saying], "Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured. And excellent is the final abode."﴾ [al-Ra'd: 23-24].

The good news at the time of death and at the entry into Paradise is through one gate, because it is good news of goodness after the transition to the Hereafter. From the attributes of those whom the angels take in death as good, and who are told, "Peace be upon you; enter Paradise," it is understood that those who did not possess piety, the angels do not take in that noble state, do not greet them with peace, and do not give them good news.

Exalted is He has explained this understanding in other places, such as:

• His saying: ﴿Those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves; so they will offer submission...﴾ [al-Nahl: 28], to the end of the verse,

• and His saying: ﴿Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves, they will say, "In what were you?"﴾, up to His saying ﴿and evil is it as a destination﴾ [al-Nisa': 97],

• and His saying: ﴿If you could see when the angels take in death those who disbelieved, striking their faces and their backs...﴾ [al-Anfal: 50], the verse,

and other verses besides these.

As for His saying: ﴿Whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves﴾ [al-Nahl: 28] and His saying: ﴿Whom the angels take in death while they are good﴾ [al-Nahl: 32], most of the readers other than Hamzah recited both with two upper ta's: "tatawaffahum" (تَتَوَفّاهم). Hamzah recited "yatawaffahum" (يَتَوَفّاهم) with the ya' in both places.

A notice (tanbih):

Here, exalted and majestic is He, attributed the taking in death to the angels in His saying: ﴿The angels take them in death﴾ [al-Nahl: 32], (p-374) and attributed it in (Surah) "al-Sajdah" to the Angel of Death in His saying: ﴿Say, "The Angel of Death will take you in death"﴾ [al-Sajdah: 11], and attributed it in (Surah) "al-Zumar" to Himself, exalted and majestic is He, in His saying: ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death﴾ [al-Zumar: 42], the verse. We have explained in our book (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab), in (the commentary on) Surah "al-Sajdah", that there is no contradiction between the mentioned verses: attributing the taking in death to Himself is because no one dies except by His will, as He said: ﴿And it is not for a soul to die except by permission of Allah, a decree with a specified term﴾ [Al 'Imran: 145]; and attributing it to the Angel of Death is because he is the one commanded to seize souls; and attributing it to the angels is because the Angel of Death has helpers from among the angels who draw the soul from the body to the throat, and then the Angel of Death takes it, as some scholars have said. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 36:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid the taghut (false deities)."﴾ In this noble verse, He - exalted is He and high is He - mentioned that He sent into every nation a messenger with the worship of Allah alone and the avoidance of worshipping anything other than Him.

This is the meaning of "there is no deity except Allah" (lā ilāha illā Allāh), because it is composed of a negation and an affirmation. Its negation is the rejection of all objects of worship other than Allah, exalted is He, in all kinds of worship, and its affirmation is the singling out of Him, exalted is He, with all kinds of worship, sincerely, in the manner He prescribed through the tongues of His messengers - upon them be the blessings and peace of Allah.

This meaning has been clarified extensively in the Qur'an through the way of the general and the specific. Among the texts indicating it along with its generality is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me﴾ [al-Anbiya' 25], and His saying: ﴿And ask those We sent before you of Our messengers: Did We appoint deities other than the Most Merciful to be worshipped?﴾ [al-Zukhruf 45], and similar verses.

Among the texts indicating it along with its specificity regarding individual prophets and their nations is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, We sent Noah to his people, and he said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him"﴾ [al-A'raf 59], and His saying: ﴿And to 'Ad, their brother Hud. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him"﴾ [al-A'raf 65], and His saying: ﴿And to Thamud, their brother Salih. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him"﴾ [al-A'raf 73], and His saying: ﴿And to Madyan, their brother Shu'ayb. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him"﴾ [al-A'raf 85], along with other verses.

Know that everything worshipped besides Allah is a taghut, and the worship of Allah does not benefit except on the condition of avoiding the worship of anything else, as He, exalted is He, explained by His saying: ﴿So whoever disbelieves in the taghut and believes in Allah has grasped the most trustworthy handhold﴾ [al-Baqarah 256], and His saying: ﴿And most of them do not believe in Allah except while associating others with Him﴾ [Yusuf 106], along with other verses.

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So among them are those whom Allah guided, and among them are those upon whom error was justly decreed.﴾ In this noble verse, He - exalted is He - mentioned that among the nations to which messengers were sent with monotheism, some are fortunate and some are wretched. The fortunate among them: Allah guides him to follow what the messengers brought; and the wretched among them: the Book precedes for him, so he denies the messengers and disbelieves in what they brought. The call to the religion of truth is general, while granting success to guidance is specific, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And Allah invites to the Abode of Peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path﴾ [Yunus 25]. His saying "so among them" [al-Nahl 36] means: among the nations mentioned in His saying "in every nation a messenger" and His saying "whom Allah guided," meaning: He granted him success in following what the messengers brought. The pronoun in the accusative, which is the link connecting the relative clause to its antecedent, is omitted, meaning: "so among them is he whom Allah guided." This is in accordance with His saying in the Alfiyya:

"And omission is frequent and clear among them in a connected pronoun if it is in the accusative of a verb or a participle, like 'whom We hope He grants' (man narju yahab)."

His saying: ﴿and among them are those upon whom error was justly decreed﴾ [al-Nahl 36] means: it was necessitated and obligated for him, because of what preceded in Allah's knowledge that he would end up in wretchedness. By "error" is meant departing from the path of Islam into disbelief.

This meaning has been explained by Him, exalted is He, in other verses, such as His saying: ﴿It is He who created you, and among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer﴾ [al-Taghabun 2], His saying: ﴿So among them is one wretched and one fortunate﴾ [Hud 105], and His saying: ﴿A party in Paradise and a party in the Blaze﴾ [al-Shura 7], along with other verses.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 38:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they swore by Allah with their most emphatic oaths that Allah will not resurrect those who die. Yes! [It is] a promise binding upon Him, in truth﴾. In this noble verse, He - exalted is He - mentioned that the disbelievers swore with their most emphatic oaths - i.e., they exerted themselves in swearing (jahd al-aymān) - and intensified their oaths that Allah does not resurrect those who die. Allah - exalted is He - refuted them in this by His saying: ﴿Yes! [It is] a promise binding upon Him, in truth﴾ [al-Nahl: 38]. He repeated in many verses this meaning mentioned here, concerning their denial of resurrection (al-ba'th) and His refutation of them in that, such as:

• His saying: ﴿Those who disbelieve claim that they will never be resurrected. Say: Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected...﴾ [al-Taghabun: 7], to the end of the verse;

• and His saying: ﴿As We began the first creation, We will repeat it - a promise binding upon Us. Indeed, We are ever doing [it]﴾ [al-Anbiya': 104];

• and His saying: ﴿And he presents to Us an example and forgets his [own] creation. He says: Who will give life to bones while they are decayed? Say: He will give them life who produced them the first time. And He is, of all creation, Knowing﴾ [Ya-Sin: 78, 79];

• and His saying: ﴿They will say: Who will restore us? Say: He who originated you the first time﴾ [al-Isra': 51].

And verses of this kind are very numerous.

As for His saying: "Yes" [al-Nahl: 38], it is a negation of their negation of resurrection, as we have mentioned. And His saying: "a promise" (wa'dan) is a verbal noun (maṣdar) emphasizing what "Yes" (balā) indicates, because "balā" indicates the negation of their saying: "Allah will not resurrect those who die." And the negation of this negation is an affirmation, its meaning being: "You will surely be resurrected." This resurrection, indicated by affirmation through the word "Yes," contains the meaning of Allah's promise that it will occur. Thus His saying "a promise" [al-Nahl: 38] emphasizes it.

And His saying: "in truth" (ḥaqqan) is also a verbal noun, i.e., Allah promised this as a promise, and He made it binding (ḥaqqahu ḥaqqan), and it is also emphasizing what "Yes" indicates.

The lam in His saying: ﴿that He may make clear to them that about which they differ﴾ [al-Nahl: 39], and in His saying: ﴿and that those who disbelieve may know﴾ [al-Nahl: 39], to the end of the verse, is connected to His saying "Yes," i.e., He resurrects them so that He may make clear to them... etc. The pronoun in His saying "to them" refers back to "those who die," because it encompasses both believers and disbelievers.

Some scholars said: the lam in both places is connected to His saying: ﴿And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger﴾ [al-Nahl: 36], to the end of the verse, i.e., We sent him so that he might make clear to them... etc. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 40:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Our word to a thing when We intend it is only that We say to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ In this noble verse He - exalted and most high - mentions that nothing can resist His power, and that when He says to a thing "Be," it is, without delay. This is because the disbelievers, when they ﴿swore by Allah their most emphatic oaths that Allah will not resurrect those who die﴾ [an-Nahl: 38], Allah refuted their lie with His saying: ﴿Yes, it is a promise binding upon Him, true﴾, and made clear that He is capable of everything, and that whenever He says to a thing "Be," it is.

He clarified this meaning in other places, such as His saying in response to the one who said: ﴿Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 78]: ﴿Indeed, His command when He intends a thing is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [Ya-Sin: 82].

He also made clear that He does not need to repeat His saying "Be". Rather, when He says to a thing "Be" once, it happens in less time than the blink of an eye, in His saying: ﴿And Our command is but one, like a glance of the eye﴾ [al-Qamar: 50]. A similar statement is His saying: ﴿And the matter of the Hour is but like a glance of the eye, or it is nearer. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent﴾ [an-Nahl: 77]. And the Most High said: ﴿Indeed, the example of Jesus to Allah is like the example of Adam. He created him from dust, then said to him, "Be," and he was﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 59], and the verse continues. And He said: ﴿Your creation and your resurrection are not but like that of a single soul﴾ [Luqman: 28], along with other verses to this effect.

The Most High referred to the intended thing before its occurrence by the name "thing," because the certainty of its occurrence is like its actual occurrence. So the verse does not conflict with applying the name "thing" specifically to what exists rather than to what does not exist. For since it has preceded in Allah's knowledge that this thing will come into existence, and that He will say to it "Be" and it will be, its certain occurrence has the standing of its occurrence. Or [the answer is that] He applied the name "thing" to it in view of its expected existence, like calling pressed juice "wine" in His saying: ﴿Indeed, I see myself pressing wine﴾ [Yusuf: 36], considering what it will become in its later state.

Ibn 'Amir and al-Kisa'i read this letter as "fa-yakuna" [an-Nahl: 40] with a fatha on the nun, in the accusative by coordination with His saying "an naqula" (that We say). It was also said that it is in the accusative by an implied "an" after the fa' that follows the imperative. The rest read it in the nominative, as the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: "fa-huwa yakun" (so it is). Indeed, one who said the following did well:

*When Allah intends a matter, He only says to it "Be" in a single utterance, and it is.*

The lam in His saying "li-shay'" (to a thing) and in His saying "lahu" (to it) is for communication (al-tabligh). This was said by Abu Hayyan.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 44:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Reminder (al-dhikr) that you may make clear to mankind what has been sent down to them, and that they may give thought﴾, the intended meaning of "the Reminder" (al-dhikr) in this verse is the Qur'an, like His saying: ﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed We will be its guardian﴾ [al-Hijr: 9].

In this verse, He—exalted is He and high is His majesty—has mentioned two of the wisdoms behind the sending down of the Qur'an upon the Prophet (ﷺ):

The first: that he should make clear to people what has been sent down to them in this Book of commands and prohibitions, promise and warning, and the like. He has also stated this wisdom in other places, like His saying: ﴿And We have not sent down to you the Book except that you may make clear to them that about which they differ﴾ [al-Nahl: 64], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth that you may judge between the people﴾ [al-Nisa': 105], and the verse continues.

The second wisdom: is reflection upon its verses and taking admonition from them, as He said here: ﴿and that they may give thought﴾ [al-Nahl: 44]. He has also stated this wisdom in other places:

• like His saying: ﴿A Book which We have sent down to you, blessed, that they may reflect upon its verses and that those of understanding may be reminded﴾ [Sad: 29],

• and His saying: ﴿Then do they not reflect upon the Qur'an? And if it had been from other than Allah, they would have found within it much contradiction﴾ [al-Nisa': 82],

• and His saying: ﴿Then do they not reflect upon the Qur'an, or are there locks upon their hearts?﴾ [Muhammad: 24],

and other verses besides these.

Al-Shinqiti's commentary on Surah 16, verse 45:

Allah, Exalted and Majestic is He, rebukes those who commit evil deeds, including disbelief and acts of disobedience, yet still feel secure from Allah's punishment and do not fear His painful seizure or His severe assault, though He is able to cause the earth to swallow them and to destroy them with various kinds of punishment. Al-khasf (causing to sink) is the earth swallowing the one it sinks with and settling down with him, downward, as Allah did to Qarun. Allah said of him: ﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home﴾ [al-Qasas: 81]. This meaning is explained in many places:

• Such as His saying: ﴿Are you secure from the One in the heaven that He will not cause the earth to swallow you, and then it shakes? Or are you secure from the One in the heaven...﴾ [al-Mulk: 16-17].

• And His saying: ﴿Are you secure that He will not cause the side of the land to swallow you, or send against you a storm of stones, and then you will not find for yourselves any protector?﴾ [al-Isra: 68].

• And His saying: ﴿Do they feel secure from the plan of Allah? None feels secure from the plan of Allah except the losing people﴾ [al-A'raf: 99].

We have already presented a portion of this in the beginning of "Surat al-A'raf".

The scholars differed over the i'rab (grammatical analysis) of "al-sayyi'at" [al-Nahl: 45] in this noble verse. Some scholars said: it is an adjective (na't) of an omitted verbal noun (masdar), meaning: they devised evil schemes, i.e., ugly deeds of intense ugliness, as Allah mentioned about them in His saying: ﴿And when those who disbelieved plotted against you, to restrain you, or kill you, or expel you﴾ [al-Anfal: 30]. Other scholars said: it is a direct object (maf'ul bih) of "makarū" (they plotted), by way of tadmin (implicit meaning: verb carrying the sense of another), with "makarū" taken to mean "fa'alū" (they did). This is, in my view, the closest of the grammatical possibilities. It has also been said: it is a direct object of "amina" (felt secure), meaning: did those who plot feel secure from the evil consequences, i.e., the severe punishments that will distress them when they descend upon them. Al-Zamakhshari mentioned the first possibility, and Ibn 'Atiyya mentioned the last two. Abu Hayyan mentioned all of them in "al-Bahr al-Muhit".

Warning.

Everything in the Qur'an that has a hamza of interrogation followed by the conjunction waw or its fa', such as His saying: ﴿Shall We then turn away the reminder from you altogether?﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 5], ﴿Have they not seen what is before them and behind them?﴾ [Saba': 9], ﴿Were not My verses recited to you?﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 31], and so on, has two well-known possibilities according to the scholars of Arabic grammar:

The first: both the fa' and the waw are conjunctions linking what follows to an omitted element indicated by the context. For example, you might say: "Shall We let you go, and so turn away the reminder from you altogether?" "Are they blind, so they did not see what is before them?" "Did My verses not come to you, so were they not recited to you?" And so on. Ibn Malik alluded to this possibility in the Alfiyya (Khulasa) with his words:

"Omitting the anchor (matbu') that appears here is permitted, and your conjoining a verb to a verb is correct."

The point of evidence is in the first half, not the second.

The second possibility: both the fa' and the waw are conjunctions linking the sentence introduced by the interrogative hamza to what precedes it, except that the interrogative hamza has shifted from its place and come before the fa' and the waw, though in meaning it comes after them. It has moved forward in wording from its position in meaning, because interrogation has the front position in speech.

From this you know that in the words of Allah in this verse, ﴿Then do those who plotted evil deeds feel secure...﴾ [al-Nahl: 45], there are the two possibilities mentioned. According to the first, the meaning is: Are those who plotted evil deeds ignorant of Allah's threat of punishment? ﴿Then do those who plotted evil deeds feel secure...﴾, and so on. According to the second, the meaning is: "So, do those who plotted evil deeds feel secure...", where the fa' is a conjunction linking the sentence introduced by the interrogative. The first is the more apparent. And Allah knows best.

Allah's saying: ﴿Merciful. Have they not considered what things Allah has created…﴾ and the rest of the verse. The explanation of this verse and similar verses has already been given in Surat ar-Ra'd.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 51:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Allah said: Do not take two gods. He is only one God, so fear Me alone.﴾ In this noble verse, Allah, Majestic and Exalted, forbade all of mankind from worshipping any other god besides Him, and informed them that the one deserving to be worshipped alone is One. Then He commanded them to fear Him (ar-rahbah), that is, to fear Him alone, because He is the One in whose hand is harm and benefit, and there is no one who benefits or harms besides Him.

He clarified this meaning in many verses:

• Such as His saying: ﴿So flee to Allah. Indeed, I am to you from Him a clear warner. And do not set up with Allah another god. Indeed, I am to you from Him a clear warner.﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 50-51],

• And His saying: ﴿[Who set up with Allah another god, so cast him into the severe punishment.]﴾ [Qaf: 26],

• And His saying: ﴿Do not set up with Allah another god, lest you sit reproached and forsaken.﴾ [al-Isra': 22],

• And His saying: ﴿And do not set up with Allah another god, lest you be thrown into Hell, blameworthy and banished.﴾ [al-Isra': 39].

And Allah, Majestic and Exalted, made clear in other places the impossibility of the plurality of gods by reason:

• Such as His saying: ﴿Had there been in them gods other than Allah, they would have been ruined.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 22],

• And His saying: ﴿And there was not with Him any other god; otherwise, each god would have taken what he created, and some of them would have overcome others. Exalted is Allah above what they describe. [He is] Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, so exalted is He above what they associate.﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 91-92],

• And His saying: ﴿Say: Had there been with Him gods as they say, they would have sought a way to the Owner of the Throne.﴾ [al-Isra': 42]. The verses on His being worshipped alone are very numerous, so we will not lengthen the discussion with them.

In His saying ﴿and fear Me alone (wa-iyyaya farhabun)﴾ He placed the object before the verb to indicate restriction (al-hasr). It has been established in the principles of jurisprudence, in the discussion of "mafhum al-mukhalafah" (implicature by contrast), and in the science of meanings (al-ma'ani), in the discussion of restriction (al-qasr), that fronting the object (taqdim al-ma'mul) is one of the forms of restriction. That is: fear Me alone, and do not fear anyone other than Me. This restriction indicated here by fronting the object, Allah, Majestic and Exalted, clarified in other places:

• Such as His saying: ﴿So do not fear the people, but fear Me﴾ (the verse) [al-Ma'idah: 44],

• And His saying: ﴿[Those] who convey the messages of Allah and fear Him and do not fear anyone except Allah﴾ (the verse) [al-Ahzab: 39],

• And His saying: ﴿Indeed, the mosques of Allah are maintained only by one who believes in Allah and the Last Day, establishes prayer, gives zakah, and fears none but Allah﴾ (the verse) [at-Tawbah: 18],

• And His saying: ﴿That is only Satan instilling fear of his allies, so do not fear them but fear Me, if you should be believers﴾ [Al 'Imran: 175],

and other verses besides these.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And to Him belongs religion (dīn), perpetually﴾. Here, religion (dīn) means obedience. For this reason, God's commands and prohibitions are called dīn, as in His saying:

• ﴿Indeed, the religion (dīn) with God is Islam﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 19],

• and His saying: ﴿And I have approved Islam as your religion (dīn)﴾ [al-Māʾidah: 3],

• and His saying: ﴿And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion (dīn), it will never be accepted from him﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 85].

The meaning of dīn in these verses is obedience to God by carrying out all His commands and avoiding all His prohibitions. From dīn in the sense of obedience is the saying of ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm in his Muʿallaqah:

*Days of ours, bright and noble, when we disobeyed the king in them, refusing to submit (an nadīna) to him.*

That is, we disobeyed him and refused to submit to him, i.e., to obey him. His saying ﴿wāṣiban﴾ [al-Naḥl: 52] means perpetual, i.e., to Him, exalted is He, belongs obedience, submission and humility perpetually. This is because His authority never weakens, He is never deposed from His authority, He never dies or is overcome, and no state changes for Him, unlike the kings of this world. One of them is obeyed, holds power and rule, and people fear him and hope for what he has for a period of time, then he is deposed or dies, or is humbled after might and brought low after elevation, so that no one obeys him anymore and no one cares for him. Glory be to Him who has not taken a son, who has no partner in dominion, and who has no protector out of weakness. Magnify Him with full magnification.

This meaning, which the implication of the verse points to, He, exalted is He, has explained in other places, such as:

• His saying: ﴿Say: O Allah, Owner of sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will, and You take sovereignty away from whom You will. You honour whom You will, and You humble whom You will﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 26],
