The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):
His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And from the fruits of the palm trees and grapes you take from them an intoxicant and good provision﴾.
This noble verse indicates that the intoxicant made from the fruits of the palm trees and grapes is not objectionable, because Allah bestowed it as a favour upon His servants in the surah of favours, which is Surah "al-Nahl."
Allah the Exalted has prohibited khamr by His saying: ﴿Intoxicants, gambling, idols and divining arrows are an abomination from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may be successful﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 90], since He described it as an abomination, as from the work of Satan, commanded avoiding it, and linked to it the hope of success. It is understood from this that whoever does not avoid it will not succeed, and this is so. The Prophet (ﷺ) has clarified that everything that veils the intellect is khamr, that every intoxicant is forbidden, and that whatever its large quantity intoxicates, its small quantity is forbidden.
The answer is evident: the verse prohibiting khamr abrogates His saying: ﴿you take from it an intoxicant﴾, and its abrogation of it is the verified position, contrary to what many of the usulis claim, that the prohibition of khamr is not an abrogation of its original permissibility, because its original permissibility is a rational permissibility, known among the usulis as the original exemption (al-bara'ah al-usuliyyah), also called continuity of the original state of non-existence (istishab al-'adam al-asli).
Rational permissibility is not among the legal rulings (ahkam shar'iyyah), so that its removal would be abrogation. Had its removal been abrogation, every legal obligation in the Shari'ah would be abrogating the original exemption from that obligation. On the point that rational permissibility is not among the legal rulings, he indicated in Maraqi al-Su'ud by his saying:
"What has been taken from rational permissibility is not the legal kind."
He also indicated that the prohibition of khamr is not an abrogation of its permissibility, because it was rational permissibility and not among the legal rulings, so that its removal would be abrogation, by his saying:
"He permitted it at the beginning of Islam as an exemption that is not among the rulings."
We said that the verified position is that the prohibition of khamr abrogates its permissibility, because His saying: ﴿you take from it an intoxicant﴾ indicates the legal permissibility of khamr, so removing this permissibility indicated by the Qur'an is the removal of a legal ruling, and so it is abrogation beyond doubt. Its permissibility could only be rational before the revelation of this verse, as is evident.
It is known among scholars that four verses of the Book of Allah were revealed concerning khamr:
The first: this verse, which indicates its permissibility.
The second: the verse in which some of its harms are mentioned, and in which it is stated that it has benefits but its sin is greater than its benefit, which is His saying: ﴿Say: In both is great sin and benefits for people, but their sin is greater than their benefit﴾ [al-Baqarah: 219]. Some people drank it after its revelation for the benefits mentioned, and others abandoned it because of the sin, which is greater than the benefits.
The third: the verse which indicated its prohibition at the times of prayer only and not otherwise, which is His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you say﴾ [al-Nisa': 43].
The fourth: the verse which prohibited it absolutely and definitively, which is His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed khamr and gambling...﴾ to His saying: ﴿So will you not desist?﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 90-91]. And Allah knows best.
As for the view of one who claims that sakar means vinegar or taste, as chosen by Ibn Jarir and Abu 'Ubaydah, or that it is vinegar, then there is no difficulty in the verse.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 68:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And your Lord inspired the bee﴾, the verse. The meaning of ī'hā' (inspiration, wahy) here is ilhām (inspiration/instinctive guidance). The Arabs use īhā' for informing something covertly; for this reason they apply it to indication (ishārah), to writing (kitābah), and to ilhām. Accordingly, Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And your Lord inspired the bee﴾ [an-Nahl: 68], meaning: He inspired it (alhamahā). And He said: ﴿So he signalled to them (fa-awḥā ilayhim) that they should glorify [Him] in the morning﴾, the verse [Maryam: 11], meaning: he gestured to them (ashāra ilayhim). He called His command to the earth an inspiration (īhā') in His saying: ﴿On that Day it will report its news﴾ ﴿because your Lord has inspired it (awḥā laha)﴾ [az-Zalzalah: 4, 5]. Among the uses of wahy for writing is the saying of Labid in his Mu'allaqah:

fa-madāfiʿu ar-Rayyāni ʿurriya rasmuhā khalaqan kamā ḍamina al-wuḥiyya silāmuhā

Here "al-wuḥiyya" in the verse (with a ḍammah on the wāw, a kasrah on the ḥā', and a shaddah on the yā') is the plural of waḥy in the sense of writing. Further clarification of this matter will come, God willing.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 70:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And among you is he who is returned to the most abject age, so that he knows nothing after having known. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing, All-Powerful﴾. In this noble verse, He - exalted and majestic - has made clear that among people there is one who dies before reaching the most abject age, and among them is one who lives long until he is returned to the most abject age. The most abject age (ardhal al-'umr) is its last stage, in which the senses deteriorate and speech and thought become disordered. It is described as abject because it is a state after which there is no hope of repairing what has decayed, unlike the state of childhood, which is a state from which one progresses to strength and the perception of things. He clarified this meaning in other places:

• As in His saying in Surat al-Hajj: ﴿And among you is he who is taken in death, and among you is he who is returned to the most abject age, so that he knows nothing after having known﴾ [al-Hajj: 5],

• And His saying in al-Rum: ﴿Allah is He who created you from weakness, then made after weakness strength, then made after strength weakness and gray hair﴾ [al-Rum: 54], the verse, and He also alluded to this

• by His saying: ﴿And no one is granted long life, nor is anything reduced from his lifespan, except that it is in a Book﴾ [Fatir: 11],

• and His saying in Surat al-Mu'min: ﴿Then that you may reach maturity, and then that you become elders; and among you is he who is taken before that, and that you may reach a specified term, and perhaps you will reason﴾ [Ghafir: 67].

Al-Bukhari said in his Sahih, in discussing this noble verse: "Chapter on His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And among you is he who is returned to the most abject age﴾ [al-Nahl: 70]. Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Harun ibn Musa Abu 'Abd Allah al-A'war narrated to us, from Shu'ayb, from Anas ibn Malik - may Allah be pleased with him -: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to supplicate: 'I seek refuge in Allah from miserliness and laziness, and from the most abject age, and from the punishment of the grave, and from the trial of the Dajjal, and from the trials of life and death.'" End of quotation. And from 'Ali - may Allah be pleased with him -: that the most abject age is seventy-five years. And from Qatadah: ninety years. The apparent meaning is that it has no fixed limit in years; rather it depends on the varying condition of individuals. For one who is seventy-five may be weaker in body and mind, and more senile, than another who is ninety years old. The apparent meaning of the words of Zuhayr in his Mu'allaqa:

؎ I have grown weary of the burdens of life; and whoever lives eighty years, by your father, will grow weary.
∗∗∗ That the one of eighty years has reached the most abject age.

And the saying of another supports it:

؎ Indeed, eighty, and when I reached it,
∗∗∗ it has made my hearing need an interpreter.

As for His saying: ﴿so that he knows nothing after having known﴾ [al-Nahl: 70] (i.e., he is returned to the most abject age, so that what he knew of knowledge in the days of youth disappears, and he remains knowing nothing, because his perception is gone due to the cause of senility). And Allah has wisdom in that.

Some scholars said: Learned people who act upon their knowledge are not afflicted by this senility and loss of knowledge and reason due to extreme old age. And this meaning may be inferred from some interpretations of His saying: ﴿Then We returned him to the lowest of the low﴾ ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ [al-Tin: 5-6] the verse.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 71:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Allah has favoured some of you over others in provision. Yet those who are favoured do not give up their provision to those whom their right hands possess, so that they are equal in it. Is it then the favour of Allah that they deny?﴾ The most apparent of the interpretations of this noble verse is that Allah has struck in it an example for the disbelievers: that He has favoured some people over others in provision, and among that is His favouring the owners over the owned in provision, and that the owners do not consent for themselves that the owned should be partners to them in the wealth and women and all the bounties of Allah that He has bestowed upon them (p-411). Yet despite this, they make idols partners with Allah in His right over His creation, which is the sincere worship of Him alone. That is: if you do not consent to associating your slaves with you in your wealth and your women, then how do you associate My servants with Me in My dominion?!

This meaning is supported by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He has struck for you an example from yourselves: Do you have, from among those whom your right hands possess, partners in what We have provided for you, so that you are equal in it, fearing them as you fear one another?﴾ [al-Rum: 28], and it is reinforced by the fact that "mā" in His saying ﴿so those who are favoured do not give up their provision to those whom their right hands possess﴾ [al-Nahl: 71] is negative, meaning: they do not give up their provision to them such that they would make them equal to themselves. End of quote.

So if they dislike this for themselves, how do they associate idols with Allah in worship of them, while acknowledging that they belong to Him?!! Just as they used to say in their talbiyah: "Here I am, O Allah, there is no partner for You, except a partner who is Yours; You own him and what he owns."

This noble verse is a clear text refuting the doctrine of socialism, which holds that no one should be better than another in provision. Allah has wisdom in favouring some of them over others in provision. He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world, and raised some of them above others in degrees, that some of them may take others in service﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 32]. He also said: ﴿Allah extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it﴾ [al-Ra'd: 26], and He said: ﴿The wealthy according to his means, and the straitened according to his means﴾ [al-Baqarah: 236], and other verses besides these.

Regarding the meaning of this noble verse there are two other opinions:

The first: that its meaning is that He made you differ in provision; so He gave you more than He gave those who are, in one word, human beings like you and your brothers. It would therefore have been fitting that you return the excess of what you were given to them, until you are equal in clothing and food, as was established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he commanded the owners of slaves to feed them from what they eat and clothe them from what they wear. According to this opinion, His saying, ﴿so those who are favoured do not give up their provision to those whom their right hands possess﴾ [al-Nahl: 71], is a reproach to them and a rebuke for that.

The second opinion: that the meaning of the verse is that He, may He be exalted and sublime, is the provider of both the owners and the owned together; so they are equal in His provision. Therefore the owners should not suppose that they give their slaves any share of provision; rather that is Allah's provision which He causes to reach them through their hands. The first opinion is the most apparent, and it is the view of the majority of scholars, (p-412) and the Qur'an indicates it, as we have explained. And Allah knows best.

His saying ﴿Is it then the favour of Allah that they deny?﴾ [al-Nahl: 71] is a denunciation from Allah of their denial of His favour; for the disbeliever uses the favours of Allah in disobedience to Allah, seeking help with every bounty He has bestowed upon him in His disobedience. He provides for them and grants them health, while they worship other than Him. "Jahada" in the Arabic language is transitive with the particle "bi" (bi-), as in His saying: ﴿And they denied them﴾ [al-Naml: 14], and His saying: ﴿So today We will forget them as they forgot the meeting of this their day, and as they used to deny Our signs﴾ [al-A'raf: 51]. Denial (judud) of a favour is its ungratefulness (kufran).

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 72 (part 1 of 2):

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Allah has made for you spouses from yourselves, and made for you from your spouses sons and grandchildren (ḥafadah)﴾, the verse. In this noble verse He, may He be exalted, mentions that He bestowed upon the children of Adam the greatest of favours by making for them, from among themselves, spouses of their own kind and form. Had He made the spouses of another species, affection, mutual harmony and mercy would not have come about.

But out of His mercy He created from the children of Adam males and females, and made the females spouses for the males. This is among the greatest of favours, just as it is among the greatest of the signs indicating that He, may He be exalted, is the One deserving to be worshipped alone.

He also explained in other places that this is a great blessing and that it is among His signs, may He be exalted:

• As in His saying: ﴿And among His signs is that He created for you spouses from yourselves that you may find tranquillity in them, and He placed between you affection and mercy. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought﴾ [al-Rum: 21],

• And His saying: ﴿Does man think he will be left neglected? Was he not a drop of semen emitted? Then he became a clinging clot, and He created and proportioned, and made of him two sexes, the male and the female﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 36–39],

• And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He it is who created you from one soul and made from it its mate that he might find tranquillity in her﴾, the verse [al-A'raf: 189].

The scholars differed concerning the meaning of ḥafadah (grandchildren/servants) in this noble verse. A group of scholars said: ḥafadah are the children of the children, i.e., "and He made for you from your spouses sons, and from the sons, ḥafadah." Some scholars said: ḥafadah are helpers and servants in general, and from this is the verse of Jamil:

"The maidservants hastened around them, and surrendered with their hands the reins of the camels"

i.e., the maidservants hastened in service, and al-wala'id are the servants, the singular being walidah. From this is the saying of al-A'sha:

"I burdened its unknown [rider] upon Yamani she-camels, when the drivers hastened upon their saddles"

i.e., they hastened in service. And from this is His saying in the surah of al-Hafd which was abrogated: "And to You we hasten and serve (nahfid)", i.e., we hasten in Your obedience. The surah of al-Khul' and the surah of al-Hafd, which were abrogated, are recommended by the Malikis to be recited as qunut in the Dawn prayer, as is well known.

It was also said: ḥafadah are the in-laws (akhtan), who are the husbands of the daughters, and from this is the saying of the poet:

"Had my soul obeyed me, there would have been for her many ḥafd, of those that are counted"

"But she is a soul proud against me, averse to the in-laws of the base, and disdainful."

al-Qadhur: the one who keeps far from falling into what is not fitting, distancing herself from being soiled by its filth.

The author of this commentary, may Allah pardon him, says: ḥafadah is the plural of ḥafid, an active participle from al-ḥafd, which is hastening in service and work. We have already mentioned in the introduction to this blessed book that among the kinds of clarification it contains is that within the verse itself there is an indicator showing the invalidity of some scholars' opinion concerning the verse. So we shall clarify that.

In this noble verse there is an indicator that ḥafadah are the children of the children, because His saying: ﴿and made for you from your spouses sons and ḥafadah﴾ [al-Nahl: 72] is clear evidence that sons and ḥafadah share the fact that they are from their spouses, and that indicates that they are all children of their spouses. The claim that His saying "and ḥafadah" is coordinated with His saying "spouses" [al-Nahl: 72] is not apparent. Just as the claim that they are the in-laws, and that the in-laws are the husbands of their daughters, and their daughters are from their spouses, and other opinions, are all not apparent. The apparent meaning of the Qur'an is what has been mentioned, and this is the choice of Ibn al-'Arabi al-Maliki, al-Qurtubi and others. It is known that a man's children and his children's children are, customarily, among his servants who hasten in his service. And knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted.

Note.

In His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿And Allah has made for you spouses from yourselves﴾, the verse [al-Nahl: 72], there is a refutation of the Arabs who used to believe that they married the jinn and had intercourse with them.

It is even narrated that 'Amr ibn Yarbu' ibn Handhalah ibn Malik married a sa'lah (a female ghoul) from them, and he would conceal her from the flash of lightning so that she would not see it and flee. Then one night lightning flashed and the sa'lah saw it and said: "'Amr!" and fled. He never saw her again. Therefore 'Ilba' ibn Arqam satirized the sons of the aforementioned 'Amr:

"Let Allah shame the sons of the sa'lah, 'Amr ibn Yarbu', the base of the an-nat."

"They are neither chaste nor shrewd (akyat)."

His saying "an-nat" originally was "an-nas" (people), in which the sin was replaced by a ta'. Likewise "akyat" originally was "akyas", plural of kayyis (shrewd), in which the sin was also replaced by a ta'. Al-Ma'arri, describing caravans of camels exiled from their homelands, said: when they see the glimmer of lightning they long for their homelands. So he claimed that he hides the lightning from them lest it make them yearn for their homelands, just as 'Amr used to hide it from his sa'lah:

"When a gleam appears, I cover their faces, as if I were 'Amr, and the mounts were my sa'lat."

The sa'lah is the old woman of the jinn. It has been narrated from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet ﷺ said: "One of the parents of Bilqis was a jinni."

The author of al-Jami' al-Saghir said: Abu al-Shaykh narrated it in al-'Azamah, Ibn Mardawayh in al-Tafsir, and Ibn 'Asakir. Its commentator al-Manawi said: in its chain is Sa'id ibn Bishr. In al-Mizan, on the authority of Ibn Ma'in, it is said: "He is weak." And on the authority of Ibn Musahhir: "There was no one in our land with better memory than him, but he is weak, munkar al-hadith," and then he cited from his munkar reports this report. End. And Bashir ibn Nahik was listed by al-Dhahabi among the weak narrators. Abu Hatim said: he is not to be used as a proof. And al-Nasa'i declared him trustworthy. End.

Al-Manawi also said in explaining the hadith "One of the parents of Bilqis was a jinni": Qatadah said: for this reason the back of her feet was like the hoof of a beast. And it has come in reports that the jinni was the mother, because her father, the king of Yemen, went out hunting and became thirsty. A tent was raised for him in which there was an old man, and he asked him for water. He said: "O Hasanah, give water to your paternal uncle." So she came out as if she were the sun, with a cup of ruby in her hand. He proposed to her from her father, and he (the father) mentioned that he was a jinni, and married her to him on condition that if he asked her about anything she had done, it would be divorce. She bore him a male child, and he had not been reminded of this before, so she slaughtered him, and he grieved over it and feared that he would ask her and she would be separated from him. Then she bore Bilqis, and she showed cheerfulness; he was troubled and could not refrain from asking her, and she said: "This is my reward from you! I have personally committed the killing of my son for your sake!" That was because her father used to eavesdrop, and he heard the angels saying: "When the boy reaches puberty he will slaughter you." Then he eavesdropped again on this one and heard them extolling her status and describing her kingdom. "This is separation between me and you," and he never saw her again. This is the substance of what Ibn 'Asakir narrated on the authority of Yahya al-Ghassani. End quote from al-Manawi's commentary on al-Jami' al-Saghir.

Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir of Surah al-Nahl: Bilqis's father, namely al-Sarh ibn al-Hudhad ibn Shurahil, was a king of great standing. He used to say to the kings of the outlying regions: "None of you is a equal (kufu') to me," and he refused to marry any of them. So they married him to a woman from the jinn called Rayhanah daughter of al-Sakan, and she bore him Bilqimah, who is Bilqis, and he had no child other than her.

Abu Hurayrah said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "One of the parents of Bilqis was a jinni." ... It is said that the reason for her father's marriage to a jinn was that he was a vizier to a tyrannical king who used to seize the wives of his subjects, and the vizier was jealous and did not marry. Once on the road he accompanied a man he did not know, who said: "Do you have a wife?" He said: "I will never marry. Our land's king seizes women from their husbands." The man said: "If you marry my daughter, he will never seize her." He said: "But he will seize her!" The man said: "We are a people of the jinn; he cannot prevail over us." So he married his daughter, and she bore him Bilqis, along with other reports.

Al-Qurtubi also said: Wuhayb ibn Jarir ibn Hazim narrated, on the authority of al-Khalil ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Uthman ibn Hadir, who said: Bilqis's mother was from the jinn; she was called Bil'imah daughter of Shaysan.

The author of this commentary, may Allah pardon him, says: The apparent position is that the hadith concerning "One of the parents of Bilqis was a jinni" is weak. Likewise, none of the reports related on this subject is established.

* *

Issue.

Scholars differed concerning the permissibility of marriage between the children of Adam and the jinn. A group of the people of knowledge prohibited it, and some permitted it.

Al-Manawi (in his commentary on al-Jami' al-Saghir) said: In the Siraji Fatawa of the Hanafis: marriage between humans and jinn, and the human-water (beings), is not permitted, due to the difference of species. In the Fatawa of al-Barizi of the Shafi'is: intermarriage between them is not permitted. Ibn al-'Imad preferred its permissibility. End.

Al-Mawardi said: This is repugnant to reason, because of the difference between the two species and the divergence of their natures; for the human is corporeal, while the jinni is spiritual. This one is of clay like pottery, and that one is of smokeless fire, so mingling despite this disparity is impossible, and procreation despite this difference is prohibited. End.

Ibn al-'Arabi al-Maliki said: Their marriage is permissible by reason; if it is authentically transmitted by text, then so be it.

The author of this commentary, may Allah pardon him, says: I know of no text in the Book of Allah or in the Sunnah of His Prophet ﷺ indicating the permissibility of marriage between humans and jinn. Rather, what may be inferred from the apparent meanings of the verses is its impermissibility. His saying in this noble verse: ﴿And Allah has made for you spouses from yourselves﴾, the verse [al-Nahl: 72], bestowing favour upon the children of Adam by making their spouses of their own kind and species, implies that He did not make for them spouses who differ from them as humans differ from jinn, and this is evident.

This is supported by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And among His signs is that He created for you spouses from yourselves that you may find tranquillity in them, and He placed between you affection and mercy﴾ [al-Rum: 21]. His saying "that He created for you spouses from yourselves," in the context of bestowing favour, indicates that He did not create for them spouses from other than themselves. This is confirmed by what is established in the principles of jurisprudence: "an indefinite noun in a context of favour is general." So His saying "made for you from yourselves spouses" [al-Nahl: 72] is an indefinite plural in a context of favour, and so it is general; and when it is general, that indicates the restriction of the spouses created for us to those who are from ourselves, i.e., of our kind and form. Although some people of jurisprudence claimed that "indefinite plurals in affirmative contexts are forms of generality," the verified position is that in affirmative contexts they are not general, and this is the view adopted in Maraqi al-Su'ud, where he said in enumerating the issues in which generality is least sound:

"Among them is the indefinite plural by custom, and that to which the consensus inclined."

But in a context of favour, the indefinite noun is general. It has been established in the principles that "an indefinite noun in a context of favour is general," as in His saying: ﴿And We sent down from the sky pure water﴾ [al-Furqan: 48], i.e., every water descending from the sky is pure. Likewise an indefinite noun in a context of negation, condition or prohibition, as in His saying: ﴿You have no god other than Him﴾ [al-A'raf: 59]; and His saying: ﴿And if any one of the polytheists﴾, the verse [al-Tawbah: 6]; and His saying: ﴿And do not obey from among them a sinner or a disbeliever﴾, the verse [al-Insan: 24]. And he finds support for this in His saying: ﴿And you leave what your Lord has created for you of your spouses. Rather, you are a transgressing people﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 166]. For it indicates in general that their abandoning what Allah created for them of spouses, and their transgressing to other than it, deserves blame, although the primary reproach and rebuke concern the abomination of sodomy; because the beginning of the speech is: ﴿Do you approach males from among the worlds?﴾ ﴿And you leave what your Lord has created for you of your spouses﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 165–166], for He rebuked them for two matters: one of them is approaching males, and the second is abandoning what their Lord created for them of their spouses.

The preceding verses have shown that what He created for them as spouses (azwaj) is that which comes from their own selves, i.e., of their own kind and form, as in His saying: ﴿And Allah has made for you spouses from yourselves﴾ [al-Nahl: 72], and His saying: ﴿And among His signs is that He created for you spouses from yourselves﴾ [al-Rum: 21], and so on. This indicates that He did not make for them spouses from other than themselves. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 73:

(p-417) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they worship besides Allah that which owns for them no provision from the heavens and the earth, nor are they able [to do anything].﴾ In this noble verse, He, may He be glorified and exalted, mentions that the disbelievers worship besides Allah that which does not own for them any provision from the heavens, by sending down rain, nor from the earth, by causing plants to grow. He emphasizes the powerlessness of their objects of worship in this respect by saying "nor are they able," meaning they are not able to provide sustenance; and the capability is negated from them entirely, because they are inanimate matter that has no capacity for any ability whatsoever.

What is understood from the noble verse is that it is not valid to worship anyone except the One who provides sustenance for creation, because their eating is from His provision, and worshipping other than Him is manifest disbelief to every person of reason. This meaning understood from this noble verse was clarified by Him, may He be glorified and exalted, in other places, such as:

• His saying: ﴿Indeed, those whom you worship besides Allah do not possess for you any provision. So seek provision from Allah, and worship Him, and be grateful to Him. To Him you will be returned.﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 17],

• And His saying: ﴿Or who is it that could provide for you if He withheld His provision? But they persisted in arrogance and aversion.﴾ [al-Mulk: 21],

• And His saying: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me. I do not want from them any provision, nor do I want that they should feed Me. Indeed, Allah is the Provider, the Possessor of strong force, the Firm.﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 56–58],

• And His saying: ﴿Say, "Is it other than Allah I should take as a protector, the Originator of the heavens and the earth, while He feeds and is not fed?"﴾,

• And His saying: ﴿And enjoin prayer upon your family and be steadfast therein. We do not ask you for provision; We provide for you. And the best outcome is for righteousness.﴾ [Ta-Ha: 132],

• And His saying: ﴿Is there any creator other than Allah who provides for you from the sky and the earth?﴾ [Fatir: 3] — the verse,

• And His saying: ﴿Say, "Who provides for you from the sky and the earth?"﴾ [Yunus: 31] — the verse,

and other verses besides these.

* *

Note.

In His saying: "shay'an" [an-Nahl: 73], in this noble verse there are three grammatical analyses (wujuh al-i'rab):

The first: that His saying "rizqan" is a verbal noun (masdar), and that "shay'an" is an object (maf'ul bihi) of this verbal noun; i.e., "and they worship besides Allah that which does not own that it provide them with any sustenance." A parallel to this construction is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿or feeding on a day of severe hunger, an orphan﴾ [al-Balad: 14–15], where His saying "yatiman" (an orphan) is an object of the verbal noun which is "it'am" (feeding), meaning: to feed an orphan who is near of kin. A parallel to it from the speech of the Arabs is the saying of al-Marrar ibn Munqidh al-Tamimi:

"With the striking of swords upon the heads of a people, we removed their skulls from their resting places."

Here his saying "ru'usa qawmin" (heads of a people) is the object of the indefinite verbal noun which is his saying "bi-darbin" (with striking). To this the author of the Khulasah (Alfiyyah) alluded in his saying:

"The verbal noun that is true in action, with its verb, [governs] as object, whether annexed, unannexed, or with the definite article."

The second wajh: that His saying "shay'an" is an apposition (badal) of His saying "rizqan," based on the premise that what is meant by "rizq" is what Allah provides to His servants, not the verbal (masdar) sense.

The third wajh: that His saying "shay'an" takes the place of the absolute object (mafʿul mutlaq) of His saying "yamliku," i.e., "does not own any ownership," meaning "does not own a little ownership to provide them."

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So do not strike forth examples for Allah.﴾

In this noble verse, Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, forbids His creatures from striking forth examples for Him, i.e., making for Him likenesses and equals from among His creation, Glorified and Exalted is He far above that, a great exaltation!

This meaning is explained in other places, such as His saying: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ [ash-Shura: 11], and His saying: ﴿And there is none comparable to Him﴾ [al-Ikhlas: 4], and other verses besides these.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 77:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And the matter of the Hour is but as a glance of the eye﴾ — the verse — the most apparent of the opinions concerning it is that the meaning is: when Allah wills to bring it about, He is able to bring it in less time than the blink of an eye, because He says to a thing "Be," and it is. And this meaning is supported by His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And Our command is but one, like a glance of the eye﴾ [al-Qamar: 50].

Some scholars said: the meaning is that it is near to Him, the Exalted, like the blink of an eye, even though it is far from you; as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, they see it as distant﴾ ﴿but We see it as near﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 6, 7], and He said: ﴿And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count﴾ [al-Hajj: 47].

Abu Hayyan, in (al-Bahr al-Muhit) [al-Bahr al-Muhit, his exegesis], chose that the "aw" (or) in His saying "or it is nearer" is for vagueness toward the addressee, and in this he followed al-Zajjaj. He said: its parallel is His saying: ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more﴾ [al-Saffat: 147], and His saying: ﴿Its command came upon it by night or by day﴾ [Yunus: 24].

Allah's saying: ﴿shay'an. And He made for you hearing, sight and hearts, that you may give thanks﴾. In this noble verse, He - Majestic and Exalted - mentions that He brought the children of Adam forth from their mothers' wombs knowing nothing, and made for them hearing, sight and hearts, so that they would give thanks to Him for His blessings. We have already mentioned that "la'alla" (so that) indicates causation (ta'lil). Here it does not state whether they gave thanks or did not; but He has made clear in other places that most of them did not give thanks, as He said: ﴿But most of mankind do not give thanks﴾ [al-Baqarah: 243], and He said: ﴿Say, "It is He who produced you and made for you hearing, sight and hearts; little are you grateful"﴾ [al-Mulk: 23], along with other verses.

Caution (tanbih).

The word "al-sam'" (hearing) does not occur in the Qur'an in the plural form; rather it always occurs in the singular, even though it encompasses what is mentioned alongside it, such as "al-af'idah" (hearts) and "al-absar" (sights).

The most evident of the opinions regarding the reason it is always singular is that its origin is the verbal noun (masdar) of "sami'a sam'an", and when a verbal noun is used as a noun, it is treated as masculine and singular; as he said in the Khulasah (of Ibn Malik):

"They described with the verbal noun often, so they adhered to the singular and the masculine."

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 79:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Have they not considered the birds, subjected in the midst of the sky? Nothing holds them up except Allah. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.﴾ In this noble verse, He, majestic and exalted, mentions that His subjecting of the birds in the expanse of the sky, such that nothing holds them up but Him, is among His signs that indicate His power and His right to be worshipped alone. He clarified this meaning in other places, such as His saying: ﴿Have they not considered the birds above them, spreading their wings and folding them in? Nothing holds them up except the Most Merciful. Indeed He is, of all things, Seeing.﴾ [al-Mulk: 19].

Warning (tanbih).

The scholars of Arabic grammar have not mentioned the form fi'l (with a fatha then a sukun) among the patterns of broken plurals (jam' taksir). The author of this commentary, may Allah pardon him, says: What appears to me from induction (istiqra') of the Arabic language is that fi'l (with a fatha then a sukun) is a broken plural of fa'il used as a descriptive noun, because it frequently occurs in the language as its plural. Such is His saying here: ﴿Have they not considered the birds﴾ [al-Nahl: 79]; al-tayr is the plural of ta'ir (bird), and like al-sahb, which is the plural of sahib (companion). Imru' al-Qays said:

"Halting by them, my companions on their mounts, saying: 'Do not perish from grief, and bear up gracefully.'"

So his saying "sahbi" means "ashabi" (my companions). And like al-rakb, which is the plural of rakib (rider). Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And the riders are lower than you﴾ [al-Anfal: 42], and Dhu al-Rummah said:

"Has the caravan brought news of their partisans, or has the heart returned, from its joys, to delight?"

So al-rakb is the plural of rakib. He referred back to it with a plural pronoun in his saying: "'an ash-yaa'ihim" (about their partisans). Like al-shurb, which is the plural of sharib (drinker). From this is the saying of Nabigha Dhubyan:

"As if, emerging from the side of its flank, it were a skewer of drinkers they left behind at the place of roasting."

He referred back to al-shurb with a plural pronoun in his saying "nasuhu" (they forgot it). Like al-safar, which is the plural of safir (traveller). From this is the hadith: "Complete (your prayer), for we are a people on a journey (safar)." And the saying of al-Shanfara:

"As if their wild cattle, their hollows and their surroundings were gatherings of tribes, descending from a journey."

Like al-rajul, which is the plural of rajil (on foot). From this is the recitation of the majority: ﴿And incite against them with your cavalry and your infantry (rajilika)﴾ [al-Isra': 64], with a sukun on the jim. As for the recitation of Hafs from Asim with a kasra on the jim, the apparent view is that the kasra of the jim is assimilation to the kasra of the lam, so its meaning is the meaning of the majority's recitation. Similar to this is very common in the speech of the Arabs, so we will not lengthen the discussion with it. And knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted.

"The Exalted's saying: ﴿And He has made for you garments which protect you from the heat, and garments which protect you from your violence﴾ — the verse. In this noble verse, Allah, the Mighty and Exalted, explains His favour upon His creation: that He made for them garments (sarabil) which protect them from the heat, i.e., and from the cold, because whatever clothing protects from heat also protects from cold. What is meant by these sarabil is shirts and the like, of cotton, linen and wool garments.

He has explained this great blessing in other places as well, such as His saying: ﴿O children of Adam, We have sent down to you clothing to cover your private parts, and as adornment﴾ — the verse [al-A'raf: 26], and His saying: ﴿O children of Adam, take your adornment at every place of prayer﴾ — the verse [al-A'raf: 31], i.e., that adornment is the good clothing which Allah created for them. His saying here: ﴿and garments which protect you from your violence﴾ [an-Nahl: 81], what is meant by them is coats of mail and the like, which protect the wearer from the impact of weapons and keep him safe from their harm.

He has also explained this great blessing, and the deserving of the one who bestowed it to be thanked for it, in other places, such as His saying: ﴿And We taught him the making of chainmail for you, to protect you from your violence. So will you be grateful?﴾ [al-Anbiya': 80]. The application of the term sarabil to coats of mail and the like is well known. From it is the saying of Ka'b ibn Zuhayr:

Lofty of noses, champions whose garments are of the weaving of Dawud, in battle, are sarabil."

The commentary of al-Shinqiti on Surah 16, verse 83:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They recognise the favour of Allah, then they deny it﴾, and the rest of the verse. In this noble verse, may He be exalted, mentions that the disbelievers recognise Allah's favour, because they know that it is He who provides for them, grants them health, and manages their affairs. Then they deny this favour, so they worship others alongside Him and make them equal to Him, though those others neither benefit nor harm and avail nothing.

May He be exalted, has made this meaning clear in many verses, such as His saying: ﴿Say: "Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth? Or who controls hearing and sight? And who brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living? And who arranges the affair?" They will say, "Allah." So say, "Will you not then fear Him?"﴾ [Yunus: 31].

His saying ﴿They will say, "Allah"﴾ [Yunus: 31] is evidence of their recognition of His favour. His saying ﴿So say, "Will you not then fear Him?"﴾ [Yunus: 31] is evidence of their denial of it. Verses of this kind are very numerous.

It is narrated from Mujahid that the occasion of revelation of this noble verse was: "A Bedouin came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked him, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited to him: ﴿And Allah has made for you from your homes a place of rest﴾ [al-Nahl: 80]. The Bedouin said, 'Yes!' He said: ﴿And He has made for you from the hides of cattle tents﴾ [al-Nahl: 80], and the verse. The Bedouin said, 'Yes!' Then he recited to him, and each time the Bedouin said, 'Yes!', until he reached: ﴿Thus He completes His favour upon you that you may submit﴾ [al-Nahl: 81]. The Bedouin then turned away, and Allah revealed: ﴿They recognise the favour of Allah, then they deny it﴾ [al-Nahl: 83]."

And from al-Suddi, may Allah have mercy on him: ﴿They recognise the favour of Allah﴾, that is, the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ, ﴿then they deny it﴾, that is, they reject him and deny his truthfulness.

May He be exalted, has also made clear that the sending of His Prophet ﷺ among them is one of the blessings of Allah upon them, as He said: ﴿Certainly did Allah confer favour upon the believers when He sent among them a messenger from themselves﴾ [Al 'Imran: 164], and the verse. He made clear in another place that they met this favour with disbelief, in His saying: ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the favour of Allah for disbelief and settled their people in the abode of ruin?﴾ [Ibrahim: 28]. It has also been said: they recognise the favour of Allah in hardship, then deny it in ease. The verses indicating this have already preceded, such as His saying: ﴿So when He delivers them to the land, at once they associate others with Him﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 65], and similar verses, along with other opinions on the verse.

His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿And most of them are the disbelievers﴾ [al-Nahl: 83]. Some scholars said: its meaning is that all of them are disbelievers. He used "most" and intended "all". This was said by al-Qurtubi and al-Shawkani. Al-Shawkani also said: or he intended by "most" the sane adults, excluding children and the like. Or he intended the disbelief of denial, and not all of them were like that; rather the disbelief of some of them was disbelief of ignorance.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 84:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then they will not be permitted to offer excuses, those who disbelieved﴾. In this noble verse, Allah, exalted is He, did not specify the object of the permission in His saying ﴿they will not be permitted﴾ [an-Nahl: 84]. However, He made it clear in (al-Mursalat) that the object of the permission is excuse-making, i.e., they will not be permitted to offer excuses, because they have no excuse that could be accepted. This is in His saying: ﴿This is a day when they will not speak. And they will not be permitted, so they will not make excuses﴾ [al-Mursalat: 35-36].

(p-422) If it is said: What is the way to reconcile the denial of their excuse mentioned here with what has come in the Qur'an of their making excuses? Such as:

• His saying, exalted is He, about them: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ [al-An'am: 23],

• and His saying: ﴿We did not used to do any evil﴾ [an-Nahl: 28],

• and His saying: ﴿Rather, we had not been calling upon anything before﴾ [Ghafir: 74],

and similar verses.

The answer has several aspects:

Among them: they will make excuses until, when it is said to them, ﴿Be driven away therein, and do not speak to Me﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 108], their speech will be cut off and nothing will remain but groaning and wailing, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿The word will be fulfilled against them because of what they did, and they will not speak﴾ [an-Naml: 85].

Among them also: the denial of their excuse is meant as an excuse that has benefit. As for an excuse that has no benefit, it is like nonexistence, and in the language of the Arabs it is truly said of it that it is "nothing." For this reason Allah, exalted is He, declared that the hypocrites are mute in His saying: ﴿Deaf, dumb﴾ [al-Baqarah: 171], together with His saying about them: ﴿And if they speak, you listen to their speech﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 4], i.e., because of their eloquence and the sweetness of their tongues. He also said of them: ﴿But when fear departs, they will assail you with sharp tongues﴾ [al-Ahzab: 19]. So what He, exalted and majestic is He, mentioned of their eloquence and sharpness of tongue, together with His declaration that they are mute, indicates that speech which has no benefit is as nothing, as is clear. Hubayrah ibn Abi Wahb al-Makhzumi said:

"Indeed the speech of a man out of its place
is like arrows that fly, with no heads on them."

We have explained this in our book (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab) in several places. The sequence with "then" [an-Nahl: 84] in His saying in this noble verse: ﴿Then they will not be permitted to offer excuses, those who disbelieved﴾ [an-Nahl: 84], after His saying: ﴿And the Day We raise up from every nation a witness﴾ [an-Nahl: 84], is to indicate that their being afflicted with being prevented from making excuses, which implies total despair, is more severe than their being afflicted with the testimony of the prophets against them for their disbelief.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Nor will they be asked to make amends﴾. Know first that (istaʿtaba) is used in the language to mean seeking ʿutba (appeasement), i.e., returning to what pleases and gladdens the one who is displeased. It is also used in the language with the meaning of (aʿtaba), when one grants ʿutba, i.e., returns to what the displeased one loves and is pleased with. When you know this, know that in His saying, ﴿nor will they be asked to make amends﴾ [an-Nahl: 84], there are two closely related interpretations.

(p-423) Some scholars of knowledge said: ﴿nor will they be asked to make amends﴾ means ʿutba is not sought from them, in the sense that they are not required to satisfy their Lord, because the Hereafter is not a place of obligation, so they will not be returned to the world to repent.

Some scholars said: ﴿nor will they be asked to make amends﴾ means they will not be granted ʿutba (i.e., they will not be given reconciliation), in the sense that the ʿatab (displeasure) is not removed from them and they are not given ʿutba, which is contentment, because Allah does not be pleased with the disbelieving people. This meaning is like His saying in the reading of the majority: ﴿And if they ask to be reconciled, they will not be among those reconciled﴾ [Fussilat: 24], i.e., if they seek ʿutba, which is His contentment with them, because of the severity of their anxiety, they will not be among those granted ʿutba, which is contentment with them. Here it is in the passive form of the active participle, i.e., those who are granted ʿutba, which is contentment with them, because the Arabs say: aʿtabahu when he returned to what pleases and gladdens him. From this is the saying of Abu Dhu'ayb al-Hudhali:

"Do you grieve over death and its misfortune,
while time does not restore the joy of one who is distressed?"

I.e., time does not return to gladness the one who grieves, nor to his contentment. And the saying of al-Nabigha:

"If you were wronged, it is a servant you wronged,
and if you are the one to be appeased, one like you would be appeased."

As for the saying of Bishr ibn Abi Khazim:

"Tamim became angry that ʿAmir was killed
on the day of al-Nisar, so they were appeased with al-Saylam."

He means: we appeased them with the sword, i.e., we satisfied them with killing. This is of the kind of sarcasm, like the saying of ʿAmr ibn Ma'di Karib:

"And cavalry I advanced upon with cavalry,
their greeting among them being a painful blow."

Because killing is not appeasement, and a painful blow is not a greeting.

As for the reading of the one who reads ﴿and if they ask to be reconciled﴾ [Fussilat: 24] in the passive form, ﴿they will not be among those reconciled﴾ [Fussilat: 24] in the form of the active participle, the meaning is: if ʿutba were sought from them and they were returned to the world to act in obedience to Allah and the obedience of His messengers, ﴿they will not be among those reconciled﴾, i.e., those returning to what pleases their Lord; rather, they will return to their disbelief in which they were at first. This reading is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars﴾ [al-An'am: 28].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 85:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when those who did wrong see the punishment, it will not be lightened for them, nor will they be given respite﴾. In this noble verse, He - majestic and exalted - mentioned that when the disbelievers see the punishment, it will not be lightened for them, and they will not be reprieved, i.e., they will not be given a respite. He clarified this meaning in other places, and He explained that they see the Fire and that it sees them (p-424), and that it nearly bursts apart from the intensity of its rage against them;

• such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿If only those who disbelieved would know, at the time when they will not be able to keep the Fire from their faces or from their backs, nor will they be helped﴾ ﴿Rather, it will come upon them suddenly and overwhelm them, and they will not be able to repel it, nor will they be reprieved﴾ [al-Anbiya': 39-40],

• and His saying: ﴿And the criminals will see the Fire and will assume that they are going to fall into it, and they will find no escape from it﴾ [al-Kahf: 53],

• and His saying: ﴿When it sees them from a distant place, they will hear its raging and roaring﴾ [al-Furqan: 12],

• and His saying: ﴿When they are thrown into it, they will hear its roaring while it boils, almost bursting with rage﴾ [al-Mulk: 7-8],

• and His saying: ﴿If only those who did wrong could see, when they see the punishment, that power belongs entirely to Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 165],

and other verses besides these.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 87:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they will offer submission to Allah that Day, and what they used to fabricate will have vanished from them﴾. Their offering submission (al-salam) to Allah is their yielding to Him and their humbling themselves before Him, a submission from which no benefit will come to them, as has already been explained in His saying: ﴿Then they will offer submission, [saying], "We did not used to do any evil"﴾ [An-Nahl: 28]. The verses indicating this are many, such as His saying: ﴿Rather, they will be submitting on that Day﴾ [As-Saffat: 26], and His saying: ﴿And faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence﴾ [Ta-Ha: 111], and similar verses. We have already presented a portion of this in our discussion of His saying: ﴿Then they will offer submission, [saying], "We did not used to do any evil"﴾ [An-Nahl: 28].

As for His saying: ﴿And what they used to fabricate will have vanished from them﴾ [An-Nahl: 87], meaning: what they used to fabricate has gone away from them and perished, namely their claim that their partners would intercede for them and bring them near to Allah in closeness. As He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And they say, "These are our intercessors with Allah"﴾ ... to the end of the verse [Yunus: 18], and as His saying: ﴿We only worship them that they may bring us nearer to Allah in closeness﴾. Their going astray from them is mentioned in many verses, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they will be returned to Allah, their true Master, and what they used to fabricate will have vanished from them﴾ [Yunus: 30], and His saying: ﴿So they will know that the truth belongs to Allah, and what they used to fabricate will have vanished from them﴾ [Al-Qasas: 75]. We have already presented the meanings of "dalal" (going astray, vanishing) in the Qur'an and in the Arabic language, with their evidences.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 88:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Those who disbelieve and bar (others) from the way of Allah — We shall add to them punishment upon punishment for what they used to spread corruption﴾. Know first that "ṣadda" (to bar, to turn away) is used in the Arabic language in two ways. The first: it is used transitively, taking an object, as in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They are those who disbelieved and barred you from the Sacred Mosque﴾ . . . the verse [al-Fath: 25]. The present tense of this transitive form is "yaṣuddu" with a ḍamma, according to the regular pattern, and its verbal noun is "al-ṣadd," also according to the regular pattern. The second: "ṣadda" is used intransitively, not taking an object. Its verbal noun is "al-ṣudūd," according to the regular pattern, and in its present tense the kasra is the regular form while the ḍamma is form by transmission (samā'). Both of these are the basis of the two seven canonical readings in His saying: ﴿When your people from it turn away (yaṣiddūn)﴾ (p-426) [al-Zukhruf: 57], with kasra and with ḍamma.

Having known this, know that His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿and barred from the way of Allah﴾ [al-Nahl: 88] admits of both possibilities: that "ṣadda" is transitive, with the object omitted because the context indicates it, in accordance with His saying in the Khulasa (the poetic summary of grammar):

"And omitting a secondary element is permissible if it causes no harm, like the omission of what is stated as an answer or is restricted."

And it also admits of the possibility that "ṣadda" is intransitive, not taking an object. However, in the noble verse there are three indicators showing that "ṣadda" is transitive and the object is omitted, i.e., "and they barred people from the way of Allah."

The first: if we were to take "ṣadda" as intransitive, meaning their turning away from Islam within themselves, that would be repetition without benefit alongside His saying ﴿Those who disbelieve﴾ [al-Nahl: 88]. Rather, the meaning of the verse is: they disbelieved within themselves, and they barred others from the religion, so this is also applied to the disbelievers.

The second indicator: His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿We shall add to them punishment upon punishment﴾ [al-Nahl: 88], for this added punishment is because of their misguiding others. The punishment added upon is their punishment for their disbelief within themselves, as evidenced by His saying regarding those misguiders who misled others: ﴿that they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and some of the burdens of those whom they mislead without knowledge﴾ . . . the verse [al-Nahl: 25], and His saying: ﴿And they will surely bear their own burdens and additional burdens along with their burdens﴾ . . . the verse [al-'Ankabut: 13], as has been previously clarified.

The third indicator is His saying: ﴿because they used to spread corruption﴾ [al-Nahl: 88], for it indicates that they used to spread corruption to others along with their own misguidance. And His saying: ﴿upon punishment﴾ [al-Nahl: 88], i.e., the punishment they deserved through their misguidance and disbelief. It is related from Ibn Mas'ud that this added punishment is: scorpions whose fangs are like tall palm trees, and serpents like the necks of camels, and vipers like Bactrian camels, which strike them. May Allah protect us and our Muslim brothers from them. And Allah knows best.

[p. 427] The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And [remember] the Day We shall raise up in every nation a witness against them from among themselves, and We shall bring you as a witness against these.﴾ In this noble verse, Allah the Exalted mentions that on the Day of Resurrection He will raise up in every nation a witness against them from among themselves, who will testify against them concerning how they responded to their messenger. He also mentions that He will bring our Prophet (ﷺ) as a witness against us. This meaning is explained in other places, such as His words: ﴿How then, when We bring from every nation a witness and We bring you as a witness against these?﴾ ﴿On that Day those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth were leveled over them﴾ [An-Nisa: 41, 42]... and His words: ﴿On the Day when Allah will gather the messengers and say, "What was your response?"﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 109], and His words: ﴿We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent, and We will surely question the messengers﴾ [Al-A'raf: 6], and other verses.

It is established in the two Sahihs (of al-Bukhari and Muslim) and others, on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Recite to me." He said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, should I recite to you when it was revealed to you?" He said: "Yes, for I love to hear it from someone other than myself." So I recited Surat an-Nisa until I came to this verse: ﴿How then, when We bring from every nation a witness and We bring you as a witness against these?﴾ [An-Nisa: 41]. He said: "That is enough for now." And behold, his eyes were shedding tears. End of quotation.

His words in this noble verse: ﴿And [remember] the Day We raise up﴾ [An-Nahl: 89] is in the accusative governed by an implied verb, "remember" (udhkur). The word "shahid" (witness) in this verse is an intensive form (fa'il) in the sense of an active participle (fa'il), meaning: a witness against them from among themselves.

* *

His words: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Book as an exposition of all things﴾. In this noble verse, Allah the Exalted mentions that He sent down this great Book to His Messenger as an exposition of all things. He explains this in other places, such as His words: ﴿We have not neglected in the Book anything﴾ [Al-An'am: 38], according to the view that the "Book" here refers to the Qur'an. As for the view that it refers to the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), then the verse contains no such explanation. In any case, there is no doubt that the Qur'an contains an explanation of all things. The entire Sunnah (prophetic tradition) is included in one verse of it, namely His words: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it﴾ [Al-Hashr: 7].

As-Suyuti said in al-Iklil fi Istinbat al-Tanzil: Allah says: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Book as an exposition of all things﴾ [An-Nahl: 89], and He says: ﴿We have not neglected in the Book anything﴾ [Al-An'am: 38]. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "There will be trials." It was said: "What is the way out of them?" He said: "The Book of Allah, in which is the news of those before you, the report of those after you, and the judgment of what is between you." Al-Tirmidhi and others recorded it. Sa'id ibn Mansur said in his Sunan: Khadij ibn Mu'awiyah narrated to us from Abu Ishaq, from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: Whoever desires knowledge, let him turn to the Qur'an, for in it is the report of the first and the last. Al-Bayhaqi said: He intended by this the foundations of knowledge. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: Allah sent down one hundred and four books, and placed the knowledge of them in four: the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, and the Furqan (the Qur'an). Then He placed the knowledge of the three in the Furqan, then He placed the knowledge of the Qur'an in the Mufassal (the later short surahs), then He placed the knowledge of the Mufassal in the Opening of the Book (al-Fatihah). Whoever knows its tafsir (exegesis) is as one who knows the tafsir of all the revealed books. Al-Bayhaqi recorded it in al-Shu'ab.

[p. 428] Imam al-Shafi'i (may Allah be pleased with him) said: All that the community says is an explanation of the Sunnah, and all explanation of the Sunnah is an explanation of the Qur'an.

Some of the early scholars (salaf) said: "I have not heard a hadith except that I sought a verse for it in the Book of Allah."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "No hadith from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) reached me in its correct form except that I found its confirmation in the Book of Allah." Ibn Abi Hatim recorded it.

Ibn Mas'ud said: "When I narrate to you a hadith, I inform you of its confirmation from the Book of Allah." Ibn Abi Hatim recorded it.

Ibn Mas'ud also said: "Every knowledge has been sent down in the Qur'an, and everything has been made clear to us in it, but our knowledge falls short of what has been made clear to us in the Qur'an." Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim recorded it.

Abu al-Shaykh recorded in al-Azamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, if Allah were to neglect anything, He would neglect the speck of dust, the mustard seed, and the gnat."

Al-Shafi'i also said: "All that the Prophet (ﷺ) judged is from what he understood from the Qur'an."

I (al-Shinqiti) say: This is supported by his (ﷺ) saying: "I do not make lawful except what Allah has made lawful in His Book, and I do not make unlawful except what Allah has made unlawful in His Book." Al-Tabarani recorded it in these words in al-Awsat from the hadith of Aishah.

Al-Shafi'i also said: "No calamity befalls anyone in matters of religion except that in the Book of Allah there is evidence on the path of guidance concerning it. If it is said: Among the rulings are those established initially by the Sunnah? We say: That is in reality derived from the Book of Allah, for the Book of Allah obligates us to follow the Messenger (ﷺ) and imposes upon us the duty of acting by his word."

Al-Shafi'i once said in Makkah: "Ask me about whatever you wish, and I will inform you of it from the Book of Allah." It was said to him: "What do you say about a muhrim (one in the state of ihram) who kills a wasp?" He said: ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful﴾ [Al-Fatihah: 1]. Allah says: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it﴾ [Al-Hashr: 7]. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from Ribi ibn Hirash, from Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Follow the two after me: Abu Bakr and Umar." Sufyan also narrated to us from Mis'ar ibn Kidam, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Tariq ibn Shihab, from Umar ibn al-Khattab that he ordered the killing of a muhrim's wasp.

[p. 429] Al-Bukhari narrated, on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "Allah has cursed the women who tattoo and those who have themselves tattooed, the women who pluck their facial hair and those who file their teeth for beauty, who alter the creation of Allah." A woman said this to him, so he said: "Why should I not curse one whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cursed, and who is in the Book of Allah?" She said: "I have read what is between the two covers (of the Qur'an), and I did not find in it what you say!" He said: "If you had read it, you would have found it. Did you not read: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it﴾ [Al-Hashr: 7]?" She said: "Yes." He said: "Then he has indeed forbidden it."

Ibn Burjan said: "Whatever the Prophet (ﷺ) said is in the Qur'an, or its origin is in it, near or far. Whoever understands it understands, and whoever is blind to it is blind. Likewise, whatever he judged or decided."

Another said: "There is nothing that cannot be extracted from the Qur'an for one whom Allah grants understanding. To the extent that some of them derived the age of the Prophet (ﷺ) as sixty-three from His words in the surah of the Hypocrites: ﴿And Allah will never delay a soul when its term has come﴾ [Al-Munafiqun: 11], for it is the beginning of the sixty-third surah, and it is followed by at-Taghabun, to show the loss (taghabun) in its absence."

Al-Mursi said: "The Qur'an has gathered the knowledge of the first and the last, such that no one truly encompasses it except the One who spoke it, then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), apart from what Allah, glorified is He, has reserved for Himself. Then the greater part of that was inherited from him by the leaders of the Companions and their great ones, such as the four Caliphs, and such as Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Abbas, to the point that he said: 'If the tether of a camel of mine were lost, I would find it in the Book of Allah.' Then the Successors (tabi'un) who followed them in goodness inherited from them. Then aspirations fell short, resolve weakened, and the people of knowledge diminished and became too weak to carry what the Companions and the Successors carried of its knowledge and all its branches. So they divided its knowledge, and each group took up a branch of its branches.

A people concerned themselves with preserving its vocabulary, verifying its words, knowing the points of articulation of its letters and their number, counting its words, verses, surahs, parts, halves, quarters, and the number of its prostrations, and other matters such as enumerating similar words and matching verses, without addressing its meanings or reflecting on what it contains. They were called the reciters (qurra').

The grammarians concerned themselves with its declinable (mu'rab) and indeclinable (mabni) nouns and verbs, its governing particles and others. They expanded discussion on nouns and their modifiers, the types of verbs, the intransitive and the transitive, the forms of the writing of words, and all that is related to them, to the point that some of them parsed its difficult passages (i'rab), and some parsed it word by word.

[p. 430] The exegetes (mufassirun) concerned themselves with its wording. They found in it a word that indicates one meaning, a word that indicates two meanings, and a word that indicates more. So they applied the first to its ruling, clarified its obscure parts, and delved into preferring one of the possible meanings of the one with two meanings or of the many meanings. Each of them exerted his thought and spoke according to what his reflection required.

The jurists of the principles (usuliyyun) concerned themselves with the rational proofs in it, and the original and theoretical indications, such as His words: ﴿Had there been in them gods other than Allah, they would have been ruined﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 22], and other numerous verses. From these they derived proofs for the oneness of Allah, His existence, His permanence and eternity, His power and knowledge, and His transcendence above what does not befit Him. They named this science "the fundamentals of religion" (usul al-din).

A group contemplated the meanings of its address and found among them what implies generality and what implies specificity, and other things. So they derived from it the rules of the language, including the literal and the figurative, and they spoke about specification (takhsis), implicit reference (idmar), the explicit (nass) and the apparent (zahir), the general and the particular, the clear (muhkam) and the ambiguous (mutashabih), command and prohibition, and abrogation (naskh), and other kinds of analogy (qiyas), presumption of continuity (istishab al-hal), and induction (istiqra'). They named this discipline "the principles of jurisprudence" (usul al-fiqh).

A group applied sound judgment and true reasoning to what it contains concerning the lawful and the unlawful and the rest of the rulings. They established its principles and its branches and expounded the matter well. They named it "the science of branches" (ilm al-furu') and also "jurisprudence" (fiqh).

Another group noticed what it contains of the stories of past generations and the earlier nations, transmitted their reports, recorded their traces and events, to the point that they mentioned the beginning of the world and the first of things. They named this "history and narrative" (tarikh wa qasas).

Others took note of what it contains of wisdoms, proverbs, and admonitions that stir the hearts of men and nearly crush the mountains. From what it contains of promise and threat, warning and glad tidings, mention of death and the return, resurrection and gathering, reckoning and punishment, Paradise and Hellfire, they derived sections of admonitions and principles of restraints. They were called "preachers and admonishers" (khutaba' wa wu'az).

A people derived from what it contains of the principles of interpreting dreams, such as what occurred in the story of Yusuf: the fat cows, the dreams of the two companions of the prison, and the sun, moon and stars prostrating, and they named it "the interpretation of dreams" (ta'bir al-ru'ya). They derived the interpretation of every dream from the Book. If it was difficult for them to extract it from the Book, they turned to the Sunnah, which explains the Book. If that was difficult, they turned to wisdoms and proverbs. Then they considered the usage of common people in their address and the customs of their habits, which the Qur'an pointed to in His words: ﴿And enjoin what is customary (al-'urf)﴾ [Al-A'raf: 199].

A people took from the verses of inheritance, with their mention of the shares and their holders and other matters, "the science of inheritance shares" (ilm al-fara'id). From their mention of the half, the third, the quarter, the sixth, and the eighth, they derived "the arithmetic of inheritance shares" (hisab al-fara'id) and the questions of awl (proportional reduction of shares when the total exceeds unity). They also extracted from them the rulings of bequests (wasaya).

A people looked at the verses in it that indicate the dazzling wisdoms in the night and the day, the sun and the moon and its stations, the stars and the constellations, and other things, and they extracted "the science of timekeeping" (ilm al-mawaqit).

Writers and poets looked at what it contains of the eloquence of its wording, the marvelous arrangement, the beauty of its context and its openings, its pauses and its conclusions, the variation in address, the amplification and the brevity, and other things. From it they derived "the science of meanings, expression and figures of speech" (ilm al-ma'ani wa al-bayan wa al-badi').

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 89 (part 2 of 2):

The people of allusion (*ishara*) and the people of truth (*haqiqa*, the Sufi concept of inner reality) examined it, and there appeared to them from its words meanings and subtleties. They gave them names that they agreed upon, such as *al-ghina'* (self-sufficiency in God), *al-baqa'* (subsistence in God), *al-huduur* (presence), *al-khawf* (fear), *al-haybah* (awe), *al-uns* (intimacy), *al-wahshah* (estrangement), *al-qabd* (contraction) and *al-bast* (expansion), and what is similar to these.

These are the arts (*funun*) which the Islamic community (*al-milla al-islamiyya*) took from it.

It also contains other sciences from the sciences of the ancients, such as: medicine (*tibb*), dialectic (*jadal*), astronomy (*al-hay'a*), geometry (*al-handasa*), algebra (*al-jabr*) and *al-muqabala* (the balancing of equations), astrology (*al-najama*), and other than these.

As for medicine: its foundation rests on preserving the system of health and the firmness of strength. That occurs only through the balance of temperament (*i'tidal al-mizaj*) according to the opposing qualities (*al-kayfiyyat al-mutadadda*). He gathered this in a single verse, which is His saying: ﴿And He was, between that, a moderate course﴾ [al-Furqan: 67].

He also informed us in it of what restores the system of health after its disruption, and of the occurrence of healing for the body after its sickness, in His saying: ﴿There comes out of their bellies a drink, varying in its colours, in which is healing for mankind﴾ [al-Nahl: 69].

Then it went beyond the medicine of bodies to the medicine of hearts and the healing of breasts.

As for astronomy: within the verses of its surahs that mention the dominion (*malakut*) of the heavens and the earth, and the created beings that He scattered in the upper and lower worlds, there is [knowledge] of it.

As for geometry: it is in His saying: ﴿Proceed to a shadow having three branches﴾ ﴿Neither shady nor protecting from the flame﴾ [al-Mursalat: 30–31]. In it there is a geometric principle, which is that the triangular shape has no shadow.

As for dialectic: its verses contain proofs (*baraheen*), premises (*muqaddamat*), conclusions (*natai'j*), the method of "saying by what is implied" (*al-qawl bil-mujib*), counter-argument (*al-mu'aradah*), and other than these, a great deal. The disputation of Ibrahim is a great foundation in this.

As for algebra and *al-muqabala*: it has been said that at the beginnings of the surahs there is mention of numbers, years and days for the chronologies of past nations, and that in them is the chronology of the survival of this community, and the chronology of the duration of the world, and what has passed and what remains, some of them multiplied by others.

As for astrology: it is in His saying: ﴿or a remnant of knowledge﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 4]. Ibn 'Abbas explained it in this sense.

It also contains the foundations of the crafts and the names of the tools that necessity calls for. Among the crafts: sewing, in His saying: ﴿and they began to stitch [leaves] over themselves﴾ ... the verse [al-A'raf: 22], [and in the verses 20, 121 of the same surah]; smithing, in His exalted saying: ﴿Bring me blocks of iron﴾ [al-Kahf: 96], and His saying: ﴿And We made iron soft for him﴾ ... the verse [Saba': 10]; building, in verses; carpentry, ﴿to construct the ship﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 27]; spinning, ﴿unravelling her yarn﴾ [al-Nahl: 92]; weaving, ﴿like the spider, which takes a house﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 41]; farming, ﴿Have you considered what you plough?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 63], in other verses; hunting, in verses; diving, ﴿and the devils, every builder and diver﴾ [Sad: 37], ﴿and you extract from it ornaments﴾ [al-Nahl: 14]; goldsmithing, ﴿And the people of Musa took, after him, from their ornaments a calf﴾ ... the verse [al-A'raf: 148]; glassmaking, ﴿a palace of glass﴾ [al-Naml: 44], ﴿the lamp is in a glass niche﴾ [al-Nur: 35]; pottery, ﴿So kindle for me, O Haman, [a fire] upon the clay﴾ [al-Qasas: 38]; seamanship, ﴿As for the boat, it belonged to poor people who worked on the sea﴾ [al-Kahf: 79]; writing, ﴿taught by the pen﴾ [al-'Alaq: 4], in other verses; baking and grinding, ﴿I carry on my head bread, of which the birds eat﴾ [Yusuf: 36]; cooking, ﴿with a roasted calf﴾ [Hud: 69]; washing and fulling, ﴿and your garments, purify﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 4], ﴿The disciples said﴾ [Al 'Imran: 52], [and in the references 5/112 and 61/14], and they are the fullers (*al-qassarun*); butchery, ﴿except what you have slaughtered﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 3]; buying and selling, in many verses; dyeing, ﴿The dye of Allah﴾ ... the verse [al-Baqarah: 138], ﴿white and red streaks﴾ ... the verse [Fatir: 27]; stone-cutting, ﴿and you hew out of the mountains houses﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 149]; measuring and weighing, in many verses; and shooting, ﴿And you did not throw when you threw﴾ [al-Anfal: 17], ﴿and prepare against them whatever you can of power﴾ [al-Anfal: 60].

It also contains the names of instruments, the kinds of foods, drinks and marriageable [persons], and all that has occurred and occurs in existence, which realises the meaning of His saying: ﴿We have not neglected in the Book anything﴾ [al-An'am: 38]. The words of al-Mursi have ended, summarised with additions.

I say: The Book of Allah has encompassed everything. As for the types of sciences, there is no branch nor any question that is a foundation except that the Qur'an contains what points to it. In it is the knowledge of the wonders of creation, the dominion of the heavens and the earth, what is in the highest horizon, what is beneath the soil, the beginning of creation, the names of the famous messengers and angels, and the notable reports of past nations, such as: the story of Adam with Iblis, in his expulsion from the Garden; the child whom he named *Abd al-Harith*; the raising of Idris; the drowning of the people of Nuh; the story of the first and second 'Ad; Thamud and the she-camel; the people of Lut; the people of Shu'ayb, the first and the last, for he was sent twice; the people of Tubba'; Yunus; Ilyas; the People of the Rass; the story of Musa in his birth, in his being cast into the river, his killing of the Egyptian, his journey to Madyan and his marriage to the daughter of Shu'ayb, his speaking with Allah, the Exalted, at the side of the Mount, his being sent to Fir'awn, his departure [from Egypt] and the drowning of his enemy; the story of the calf and the people whom he took out and whom the thunderbolt seized; the story of the fighting and the slaughter of the cow; his story in fighting the tyrants; his story with al-Khidr and the people who travelled through a tunnel in the earth to China; the story of Talut and Dawud with Jalut and his killing; the story of Sulayman, his report with the Queen of Saba' and his trial; the story of the people who fled from the plague, whom Allah caused to die and then brought back to life; the story of Ibrahim in his disputation with his people, his debate with Nimrod, his placing Isma'il with his mother at Makkah, his building of the House; the story of the sacrificed [son]; the story of Yusuf, and how extensive it is; the story of Maryam, the birth of 'Isa by her, his sending and his raising; the story of Zakariyya and his son Yahya; Ayyub and Dhu al-Kifl; the story of Dhu al-Qarnayn, his journey to the rising and the setting of the sun, and his building of the barrier; the story of the People of the Cave and the Inscription; the story of Bukhtnassar; the story of the two men, one of whom had the garden; the story of the People of the Garden who swore that they would harvest it at dawn; the story of the believer of the family of Fir'awn; the story of the People of the Elephant; and the story of the tyrant who wanted to ascend to the heaven.

It also contains concerning the affair of the Prophet ﷺ: the supplication of Ibrahim for him, the good tidings of 'Isa concerning him, his sending and his migration. Among his military expeditions: the Battle of Badr in (Surat al-Anfal); Uhud in (Al 'Imran); the Lesser Badr in it; the Trench in (al-Ahzab); the Banu al-Nadir in (al-Hashr); al-Hudaybiyah in (al-Fath); Tabuk in (al-Bara'ah); the Farewell Pilgrimage in (al-Ma'idah); his marriage to Zaynab bint Jahsh; the prohibition of his concubine; the collaboration of his wives against him; the story of the slander (*ifk*); the story of the Night Journey (*isra'*); the splitting of the moon; and the sorcery of the Jews against him.
